title.proposed: Build a fire-once background job runner for Endless

description.current: A fire-once runner: when invoked, it executes any due jobs from a pluggable job registry, then exits. Repetition and scheduling live in the trigger, not the runner — session monitor fires it on each refresh today; a future long-running daemon will fire it on events, including clock ticks. Concurrency-safe across the many monitors that may fire it simultaneously via a DB ticker + compare-and-set lease, so exactly one invocation claims and runs a given due job. Jobs are defined by their own tasks and register with the runner; the runner itself knows nothing job-specific.

Decision: hide entirely (vs. filter to verify/blocked) because needs-attention is expanded by default, making the summary redundant. Trade-off: loses 'at a glance' value if multiple attention-needing children exist; revisit if needs-attention becomes collapsed by default. PROCESS LESSON: Claude initially substituted hiding for filtering (Mike's actual ask) without discussion. Mike's objection was process, not outcome — when Claude believes a different approach is better, Claude must explain trade-offs and let Mike choose, not silently substitute. Required form: 'I think X is better because Y — what do you think?' not '[ships X]'.

title.current: Add git worktrees and behavioral gate for parallel sessions
title.proposed: Add git worktrees and behavioral gate for parallel sessions

description.current: Workstream 3 of E-968. The headline feature: per-session git worktrees so concurrent sessions don't collide, plus a behavioral gate to catch topic drift. Two flavors: per-session worktrees (auto-created on session start, removed on session end) and dedicated task worktrees (for plan-bearing tasks; persist across sessions). Rust-style ownership: at most one owner at a time, transferable via .endless/worktree.lock (atomic O_EXCL claim, stale via kill -0, released on SessionEnd). Main = sacred clean integration target; 'endless worktree land' refuses dirty main. Behavioral gate: UserPromptSubmit hook injects active-task system reminder (Layer 1) plus deterministic phrase match against E-970's pivot kind (Layer 2); PIVOT word as deliberate user override; gate clearance via task add or task start (CLI verb required, not chat ack). Blocked by E-969 (plan-bearing detection), E-970 (phrase storage), E-972 (project resolution). Plan: .endless/plans/E-971.md.

title.current: Fix endless project resolution to detect main repo from inside a worktree
title.proposed: Fix project resolution from inside a worktree

description.current: Bug: when endless CLI commands run from inside a git worktree (e.g. .endless/worktrees/<id>/), events were appended to the worktree's .endless/events/ instead of main's, because event_bridge.emit_event defaulted project_root to Path.cwd(). Result: bifurcated event logs with the same project's writes split across multiple .endless/events/ directories. Discovered when another session reported strange behavior from inside the e-967 worktree; confirmed by comparing event-log file sizes between main and worktree. Fix (commit 351ec45): emit_event now looks up the project's registered path by name from the projects table and uses that, falling back to cwd only if the project isn't registered. Worktree's events file at the time of the fix had 150651 bytes of strays — reconciliation tracked separately as E-979.

Motivation: task<->decision pairs have become painfully common in this codebase (see E-957, E-958, E-975/E-976, E-977/E-978). Today, capturing rationale requires three steps: (1) make the change, (2) 'task add --type decision' with the rationale, (3) link them. Compressing that into one CLI invocation removes the friction that causes rationale to get lost in commit messages or chat instead of the task DB. Depends on E-957 (general-purpose link CLI) and E-958 (vocabulary). Acceptance: 'endless task update E-X --status verify --decision "smoke tested locally"' creates a decision task, links it to E-X, and records the rationale in one shot.

title.current: Resolve tension between event log auto-appends and clean-main precondition
title.proposed: Resolve event log auto-appends vs clean-main precondition

description.current: Architectural conflict: E-808's event log files are committed and authoritative (every CLI mutation appends), while E-971's 'worktree land' refuses dirty main. Together they make main continuously dirty and unlandable. Surfaced during E-969 work; we already had to commit a stray events JSONL just to keep main landable. Options range from auto-commit on every append, to gitignoring the log, to a narrower 'landable cleanliness' definition, to moving the log out of the working tree, to batched commits via a daemon. Full options analysis is in the analysis field.

title.current: Design sandbox/fixture pattern for tests that mutate state
title.proposed: Design sandbox/fixture pattern for tests that mutate state

description.current: Tests and verification work that mutate Endless state must run against an isolated sandbox/fixture (separate event log + DB), never against the live system. Today there is no such pattern, which forces verification work to either touch live data and require cleanup (creating the temptation for raw-SQL bypass that produced the E-979 desync — see declined E-993) or to skip mutation testing entirely. This task is BIG and needs its own planning session: scope includes how a sandbox is provisioned (temp dir? in-memory SQLite? cloned event log?), how it is selected (env var? CLI flag? context manager?), how event-sourcing invariants are preserved within the sandbox, and what the developer/agent ergonomics look like. No implementation until plan is approved. A follow-up task to add 'task clear text' / 'task clear prompt' verbs should be filed AFTER this lands — sandboxes must exist before agents get a tool that makes 'mutate live then reset' easier.

title.current: Design field separation for plan content vs analysis content on tasks

description.current: The tasks.text column has been treated as 'the plan' (planned plan-bearing detector keys off its presence), but there is no field for problem analysis, design briefs, research notes, or decision rationale — content that is long-form but not a plan. title.current: Convert endless CLI install to editable mode so source changes go live without reinstall

title.current: Build test infrastructure for click-runner tests that bypass endless-event Go binary
title.proposed: Build CliRunner test infrastructure for the Go event binary

description.current: Tests that invoke CLI commands via click.testing.CliRunner currently fail when the command shells out to the endless-event Go binary, because the Go binary connects to the system DB (or its configured path) rather than the test's isolated DB. Workaround used in tests/test_decision_flag.py: monkeypatch endless.task_cmd.add_item to insert tasks directly via SQL, skipping emit_event entirely. This works for tests that only need a task to exist, but loses fidelity: we're not actually testing that emit_event is called correctly, the event is shaped right, or the project lookup happens. Better infrastructure options: (1) build a Python-side stub for emit_event that writes the same DB row the Go binary would, configurable via fixture; (2) point the Go binary at the test DB via env var or flag; (3) accept the limitation and document the patterns.
description.proposed: Let CliRunner tests exercise commands that emit events through the endless-event Go binary against the test's isolated DB, instead of monkeypatching event emission away.

title.current: Fix hook task-start/complete regex to accept E-prefix on task IDs
title.proposed: Fix hook task-start/complete regex to accept E-prefix

description.current: The CLI's TaskIDType (src/endless/cli.py:10) accepts both 'E-1027' and '1027', but the hook's regex matchers in DEFAULT_MATCHERS (src/endless/matchers.py:75,79) only match bare digits. So 'endless task start E-1027' typed in a Bash tool is silently a no-op for the session-state side effect: StartWorkSession never fires, sessions.active_task_id stays NULL. Fix: relax both regexes to accept an optional [Ee]- prefix; capture group still extracts only digits. Two places: DEFAULT_MATCHERS and existing machine configs (decide migration vs manual edit).

title.current: Add worktree-local binary preference to endless CLI
title.proposed: Add worktree-local binary preference to endless CLI

description.current: /usr/local/bin/endless-go is a single global symlink into the MAIN checkout's bin/. Inside a worktree, the Python CLI and anything resolving through PATH get main's binary, not the worktree's candidate, so candidate Go code is not exercised by ordinary CLI use and the documented workaround is invoking ./bin/endless-go directly. Two neighbours already solved adjacent halves: E-998 points a worktree Claude session's hooks at the worktree's own bin/endless-go hook claude via its .claude/settings.json, and E-1368 made the binary self-detect the sandbox DB from cwd -- but that routes the DATABASE, not which binary runs. Approaches: (a) prepend ./bin to PATH in shell-init when in a worktree, (b) have the Python CLI auto-detect a worktree-local bin/ and prefer it, mirroring E-1368's cwd self-detection, (c) install per-worktree to alternative paths.

title.proposed: Implement safeguard against losing uncommitted work in main

title.current: Fix rebuild-db FK and UNIQUE failures from pre-E-808 backfill gap and ID reuse
title.proposed: Fix rebuild-db FK and UNIQUE failures

description.current: rebuild-db replay logs three classes of warnings: (a) task.created/task.landed FK failures where the parent or task doesn't exist in the projection - pre-E-808 tasks were inserted via raw SQL and have no task.created event to replay; (b) UNIQUE failures where the ledger has two task.created events for the same ID - root cause is PreAllocateTaskID using SELECT MAX(id)+1, which reuses the deleted task's ID when it was the highest; (c) UNIQUE failures where committed test/e2e fixture ledgers reuse real task ids 1..~150 (~36 of 47 committed segment files, per the E-1710 audit) - scrubbing those is E-1716, preventing new pollution is E-1665. All classes silently drop or corrupt rows in the projection vs the live DB. FK discovered during E-787 Phase 5; UNIQUE+ID-reuse confirmed during E-1507 verification; fixture-reuse found in the E-1710 audit.

title.current: Add post-edit commit prompt for CLI commands that mutate auto-committed files
title.proposed: Add post-edit commit prompt for auto-committed files

description.current: Per discussion (Mike, 2026-05-01) on E-1056: when a user manually edits .endless/config.json AND an AI session runs 'endless phrase add', both changes get bundled in the next 'endless worktree land' auto-commit, losing the user's manual-edit attribution. Mitigation: after CLI commands that mutate auto-committed files, prompt 'Commit this change now as a separate commit? [y/N]' (default no); if yes, runs 'git add <file> && git commit -m "<message>"' in the current worktree. Decide later: which commands trigger the prompt, default behavior, suppression flag (--no-prompt), and headless/scripted behavior. Revisit when manual-edit bundling has actually surfaced as a real complaint.

title.current: Migrate Python CLI surface entirely to Go (umbrella)
title.proposed: Migrate Python CLI surface entirely to Go

description.current: Umbrella for porting the human-facing CLI (task, worktree, and the rest) from Python to Go. The hot path is already Go behind a single consolidated binary (E-1367 superseded the multi-binary layout; the web surface was excised by E-1939). Settled: the end state is ONE binary named endless, and no transitional second command set is needed — every name the two surfaces share today is a Python shim in front of the Go implementation, so merging deletes the shim rather than reconciling a conflict. Settled: once the port starts, no new Python work lands in the files being ported (task_cmd, cli, worktree_cmd, session_cmd); anything still open at that point is re-filed against the Go implementation rather than carrying a patch with nowhere to land. Still open: whether internal plumbing (event, hook, sandbox, template, markdown) stays visible in help once the binary is user-facing. E-2084 scopes what must land and what must move first.

title.current: Design a strategy to propagate session-learned rules into the endless repo in parallel with memory
title.proposed: Design a strategy to store session-learned rules in the repo

description.current:
Per-session AI memory (~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/MEMORY.md and friends) only helps the same Claude instance with that memory directory. It does not reach: other Claude sessions on other machines, other AI harnesses (Codex, etc.), human users of endless-the-product, or future fresh sessions that haven't accumulated those rules.

Yet many learned rules are project-level — they describe how endless's workflow is meant to work, not personal user preferences. Examples surfaced in 2026-05-01 conversation:
- 'Long-form task content goes in .endless/plans/E-NNN.md attached via --text; description stays a 2-3 sentence pitch.'
- 'The session that creates a plan file owns committing it.'

Both are about endless's plan workflow. They should reach every user, not just one Claude instance.

Open question: project-specific feature, or general 'lessons' infrastructure all endless-managed projects could use? (User's global ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md already has a pattern: 'After ANY correction from the user: update ~/.claude/LESSONS.md with the pattern.' That's user-scoped. Project-scoped equivalent would be e.g. .endless/lessons/ or project-LESSONS.md.)

Considerations / things to weigh:
- Where do learnings live? .endless/learnings/<topic>.md? .endless/conventions.md? Inline in quick-start guide? Repo-level CLAUDE.md? Multiple?
- Mike's pushback (2026-05-01): 'CLAUDE.md does not work because everyone's CLAUDE.md may be different.' Repo-rooted CLAUDE.md is shared, but users may override or omit it; can't rely on it as authoritative.
- Auto-propagation vs. manual: should there be tooling (e.g. 'endless lesson add') that captures a rule and writes it to the repo? Or just a convention agents follow?
- How does an agent/user discover existing lessons? Surface in 'endless quick-start'? A new 'endless lessons' command?
- Distinguish project-level rules (apply to all who work on this project) from personal rules (apply to this user's preferences). The latter still belongs in personal memory only.
- Migration path: rules already in personal memory that should also be in the repo — how do they get there?

Origin: 2026-05-01 conversation. Mike: 'create a task for another session to work on that come up with a strategy to write learnings to the endless repo in parallel with memory. This may be unique to the endless project itself, or maybe it is a general lessons feature that all projects could use.'

Out of scope for this design task:
- Implementing the chosen strategy (file follow-up once design lands).
- Migrating existing personal-memory rules into the repo (separate task).

title.current: Fix _migrate_v5 non-idempotent swap UPDATEs flipping blocks/replaces rows on every connect
title.proposed: Fix _migrate_v5 re-flipping blocks/replaces rows each run

description.current: src/endless/db.py:_migrate_v5 contains two UPDATE statements that swap source/target on rows where dep_type IN ('needs','blocks') and where dep_type='replaces'. They have no version gate, so they run on every endless command and flip every blocks/replaces row's direction each time. Result: data corruption — at any moment, ~half of rows are in their intended direction and ~half are inverted, depending on parity of past invocations. Symptoms originally observed as inconsistent labels in 'task show' / 'task relations' / 'task detail' for the same task; the labels were correct, the underlying data was flapping. Fix: gate the swap UPDATEs on PRAGMA user_version; set user_version=5 once V5 has run. Audit existing data afterwards (5 replaces rows + 60 blocks rows). Pre-existing data corruption from past flips was repaired manually post-patch. E-863 (proper schema version migration system) is the structural fix that would have prevented this.

title.current: Skip endless-hook work when cwd is in a worktree but binary is the global one

description.current: E-998 created per-worktree .claude/settings.json so worktree-cwd Claude sessions fire bin/endless-hook. description.current: After E-1126's complete→confirm rename, the hook's PostToolUse handler clears sessions.active_task_id when Claude runs 'endless task confirm <id>' as a Bash tool call. But Python's complete_item (src/endless/task_cmd.py:1476) does the underlying DB writes and never touches the session row. If a user runs 'endless task confirm <id>' directly in a terminal — bypassing the hook entirely — the task gets marked confirmed but the session keeps pointing at it as active. Fix: have complete_item null active_task_id for any session whose active_task_id matches the just-confirmed task. Surfaced during E-1126 verification.

title.current: Detect worktree context in endless cwd-walk to avoid empty-DB autocreate
title.proposed: Detect worktree context in endless cwd-walk

description.current: When endless is invoked from inside a git worktree (e.g., .endless/worktrees/e-NNN/), cwd-walk finds the worktree's own .endless/ directory and connects to a fresh/empty SQLite there instead of the main checkout's real DB — surfaces as 'no such table: tasks'. Detect the worktree case (git rev-parse --git-common-dir or presence of .endless/worktrees/<name>/ ancestry) and either anchor to the main checkout's .endless/ or refuse with a clear error pointing at the fix. Discovered 2026-05-03 verifying E-1114 from its own worktree.

title.current: Replace SQLite traceback with actionable error when endless DB is missing or empty
title.proposed: Replace missing/empty DB traceback with actionable error

description.current: When endless connects to a SQLite file that exists but has no tables (or is missing entirely), commands fail with a raw sqlite3.OperationalError traceback ('no such table: tasks' / 'no such table: projects'). Common triggers: (a) ENDLESS_PROJECT_ROOT/ENDLESS_WORKTREE_PATH env vars from a stale esu activation pointing at a worktree's empty .endless/, (b) cwd-walk landing in a worktree whose .endless/ has no DB (see E-1158). Catch sqlite3.OperationalError at the db.query boundary and re-raise as a friendly message naming the resolved DB path, the resolution mechanism (env var vs cwd-walk), and the recovery (cd elsewhere, unset ENDLESS_*, or run init). esp itself crashes on this path too — fixing the diagnostic auto-fixes esp's UX. Discovered 2026-05-03 verifying E-1114.

title.current: Detect ENDLESS_SANDBOX in endless CLI and refuse with actionable error
title.proposed: Detect ENDLESS_SANDBOX in endless CLI and refuse

description.current: endless-sandbox enter/run exports ENDLESS_SANDBOX=<sandbox-dir>; inside that subshell every endless command that does I/O is wrong-by-construction (DB, config, verbs.json all redirected by XDG_CONFIG_HOME). Fix: one gate at CLI entry that refuses with an actionable error (name the sandbox, tell the user to 'exit') UNLESS the invoked subcommand is on an explicit allowlist (--help, --version, shell-init seed it; anything new added later must be justified in the diff). Allowlist beats deny-list because future subcommands inherit refusal automatically. Sibling of E-1160. Discovered 2026-05-03 verifying E-1114.

title.current: Document approach for clearing ENDLESS_* vars set by use.sh extensions
title.proposed: Document clearing of vars set by use.sh extensions

description.current: esf (E-1159) clears only the env vars that 'endless session use' is documented to export — currently just ENDLESS_SESSION_ID per E-1038. A user-authored .endless/extensions/use.sh (E-1014) can export arbitrary additional vars (e.g., PATH alterations, NVM_DIR, project-specific exports). esf has no way to know what an extension set, so those leak. Possible approaches to investigate: (a) symmetric extensions/forget.sh that authors maintain alongside use.sh; (b) protocol where use.sh emits a sentinel line listing what it set, captured by esu and replayed by esf; (c) snapshot env before/after esu and diff at esf time. Each has trade-offs. Maybe-task: document the design space, pick an approach if/when extension-var leakage becomes a real problem. References: E-1014 (extension hooks), E-1038 (single-var reduction), E-1159 (esf implementation).

title.current: Route shell helpers to worktree CLI via session lookup when ENDLESS_SESSION_ID set
title.proposed: Route shell helpers to the session's worktree CLI

description.current: esu/esp/esf call bare 'endless' which resolves to the global CLI. New subcommands added in a worktree (like 'session forget' from E-1159) aren't reachable via helpers until the worktree is merged and globally installed. Use.sh can route but shouldn't be a baseline requirement — users in non-endless-source projects shouldn't have to author a shell extension just for esf to work. Fix: when ENDLESS_SESSION_ID is set, helpers look up worktree_path via 'endless session show $ENDLESS_SESSION_ID --json' and route via 'uv run --directory $worktree_path endless'. Also: clearer errors when (a) helper isn't loaded — install command_not_found hook saying 'run eval $(endless shell-init) first'; (b) ENDLESS_SESSION_ID unset — say 'no active session, run esu first.' Discovered 2026-05-03 verifying E-1159.
description.proposed: When a session is active, make the esu/esp/esf shell helpers run the endless CLI from that session's worktree instead of the global install, with clearer errors when a helper or session is missing.

title.current: Fix origin/HEAD unset fallback in worktree base-branch detection
title.proposed: Fix base-branch fallback when origin/HEAD is unset

description.current: _default_base_branch in src/endless/worktree_cmd.py uses git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD, which is unset on fresh clones (it requires git remote set-head). When unset, we fall back to literal 'main', which is wrong if the repo's default is 'master', 'develop', etc. Better fallback: read init.defaultBranch from git config, or query git ls-remote --symref origin HEAD. Filed during E-971 Layer F implementation.

title.current: Rename .endless/events to .endless/db-ledger to signal DB durability
title.proposed: Rename .endless/events to .endless/db-ledger

description.current: The 'events' directory naming caused near-data-loss during E-1170's land: those JSONL files are the Endless DB write-ahead record (replay-source for DB rebuild), but their name reads as 'logs' so they were treated as discardable. 'journal' has the same problem (cf. systemd journalctl). Rename to 'db-ledger' / 'db-entries-<id>.jsonl' to force the 'authoritative database record' mental model — ledger and entries are canonical accounting terms; losing one is catastrophic in every domain that uses them. Migration spans Go writer (cmd/endless-event), Python bridge (event_bridge.py), DB replay/rebuild logic, hooks that scan the path, tests, and a one-time directory rename for existing installs with backward-compat read window. Open at plan time: keep current host-fp+sequence identifier vs. switch to UUIDs.

title.current: Record each .endless/db-ledger/ write in git immediately, not just at land time
title.proposed: Record each db-ledger write in git immediately

description.current: Today .endless/events/*.jsonl (and after E-1197, .endless/db-ledger/db-entries-*.jsonl) only get committed when 'endless worktree land' runs — they accumulate uncommitted on main between landings. Result: any session that runs endless commands fills the working tree with uncommitted database write-ahead state, which then needs cleanup before any subsequent land. Auto-commit on every event emission so each ledger write becomes part of git history immediately — premium data integrity, no risk of stash-induced loss. Optimization to evaluate at plan time: for commits that haven't been pushed to origin yet, amend successive auto-commits into a single rolling commit. Bounds the commit count without weakening data integrity (each event still becomes part of git history at write time; the amend just rewrites how recent unpushed history is grouped). Sooner-than-later priority because the current friction blocks landing.

title.current: Record verbs.json changes immediately on endless verb add
title.proposed: Record verbs.json changes immediately on endless verb add

description.current: Today 'endless verb add <name>' modifies .endless/verbs.json without committing. Result: every verb addition leaves the working tree dirty until either (a) someone manually commits, or (b) the next 'endless worktree land' bundles it into the auto-record commit. The verb registry is global config — repo-tracked so all sessions/users on this project benefit from discovered verbs, and machine-stored so verbs are available outside project context. title.current: Fix endless worktree land failing to remove worktree dir due to untracked .endless/worktree.json
title.proposed: Fix worktree land failing to remove the worktree dir

description.current: On every worktree land, the final `git worktree remove` step fails with `fatal: <path> contains modified or untracked files` because per-worktree state files in `.endless/` are intentionally untracked: `worktree.json` (companion file, never committed because committing it would rotate every worktree's contents whenever another is created/destroyed) and `worktree.lock` (ownership marker per E-971; SessionEnd hook is supposed to delete it but in practice it survives — observed on E-1186 land 2026-05-09). Related: E-1009 (gitignore both), E-1195 (review whether the lock-file model itself stays).

title.current: Design adoption-friendly handling of user-produced dirty state in main
title.proposed: Design handling of user-produced dirty state in main

description.current: Endless and Claude have hard rules (E-1199, E-1200, E-1204) against direct commits or dirty session-work state in main. End users will produce both during normal pre-endless workflows; the tooling must not block them. Detect via existing CLAUDECODE / ENDLESS_SESSION_ID env vars (no new vars). Mechanisms: (1) startup tip when main has any dirty state pointing to 'endless worktree move'; (2) 'endless worktree move' command that lifts uncommitted changes from main into a fresh worktree, leaving main clean; (3) reject pre-commit hooks as a mechanism (not composable, agreed elsewhere). Goal: zero-friction adoption — users get value without changing behavior, and behavioral shifts happen voluntarily as they see the tooling. Note: 'move' chosen over 'extract' (read as removing FROM a worktree), aligns with git's vocab via 'git worktree move'.

description.current: Per-worktree metadata files .endless/worktree.json and .endless/worktree.lock are not in .gitignore and were accidentally committed to main in commit ed83306 (.endless/worktree.json with E-1186 content). Consequences: (1) every new worktree from main inherits the stale companion; Layer F's create_task_worktree overwrites it locally, which then shows as M in 'git status' and makes 'endless worktree land' fail at the worktree-removal step; (2) the PreToolUse hook's walk-up from cwd finds the companion in main and treats main as a worktree, causing sibling sessions to claim a .endless/worktree.lock there (PID 54419 in the current case); (3) any session in main hits a 'worktree owned by another session' refusal on Edit. Fix: add both files to .gitignore, 'git rm --cached .endless/worktree.json' from main, delete the orphan .endless/worktree.lock in main. Related to E-1195 (lock ownership-model review) but distinct: this is a tracking bug, not a staleness-detection design question.

title.proposed: Rename 'task start' to 'task claim' and add 'task release'

No 'start' alias (per no-legacy-code rule) unless explicitly requested. Update verb registry, CLAUDE.md references, and test names. Relates to E-1203 (which created the refusal that makes the rename matter).

title.current: Audit FindWorktreeRoot for cross-project walk-up leak
title.proposed: Audit FindWorktreeRoot for cross-project walk-up leak

description.current: FindWorktreeRoot at internal/monitor/worktree_lock.go walks up from cwd looking for .endless/worktree.json. If cwd is OUTSIDE projectRoot's tree (e.g., /home/user/different-project), the walk-up never reaches projectRoot's dir==root termination and could find a foreign .endless/worktree.json somewhere up that tree. Callers (handleWorktreeAdoption, shouldSkipForWorktreeAt) do not validate the returned path is inside projectRoot, so foreign companions could trigger adoption of a worktree outside the registered project. Audit: trace each caller, determine whether the cross-project leak is reachable in practice, and recommend a fix (likely: add a projectRoot containment check in FindWorktreeRoot, or in each caller). Surfaced as out-of-scope during E-1219 audit.

title.current: Create .endless/worktree.json on endless task start when cwd is a git worktree without companion
title.proposed: Create worktree.json on task start in a bare git worktree

description.current: Post-E-1218, .endless/worktree.json is gitignored and not tracked in main. New worktrees created via 'git worktree add' directly (vs. 'endless task spawn' or 'endless worktree add') do not get a companion file written. As a result, 'endless task start E-NNN' refuses with 'Path X exists but does not belong to E-NNN' because it cannot find the companion at the expected location. Workaround: write the companion manually before running task start. Proposed fix: have endless task start auto-create the companion when (a) the cwd is a registered git worktree under .endless/worktrees/, (b) no companion file exists, (c) the task ID being claimed has no other registered worktree. Surfaced during E-1209 and E-1219 setup — hit it twice in one session.

title.current: Fix 'task release' to handle missing/stale/competing bindings without requiring 'current session'
title.proposed: Fix 'task release' for missing, stale or competing bindings

description.current: Today release_item REQUIRES resolving the current Endless session id, then verifies ownership against it. That breaks the explicit-ID use case: running 'endless task release E-NNN' from a non-Claude shell errors with 'Cannot resolve current session id' even when the user is unambiguously naming the task to release. title.current: Fix right-click menu to anchor at mouse cursor (capture coords at binding time)
title.proposed: Fix right-click menu to anchor at the mouse cursor

description.current: Deeper fix for the right-click menu position bug that E-1251 only superficially addressed. With E-1246`s refactor, bindings do `run-shell endless-tmux show-menu --position=mouse`, and my Go binary then invokes `tmux display-menu -x M -y S`. The `M` token is only resolvable in tmux`s original binding context — by the time `display-menu` runs from a fresh invocation inside `run-shell`, the mouse event is gone, so `M` falls back to top-left. Fix: capture `#{mouse_x}` and `#{mouse_y}` at binding time (tmux substitutes them while it still has the mouse event) and pass as numeric `--mouse-x` / `--mouse-y` flags to show-menu, which forwards them as `display-menu -x <num> -y <num>`. Bindings need double-quoted run-shell args so tmux substitutes `#{...}`.

description.current: Add `endless task bind <id>` as a new verb that binds the current session to a task for status-bar display without changing the task`s status or creating a worktree. Symmetric counterpart to `endless task release`: bind sets `sessions.active_task_id`, release clears it. Use case: a task is `assumed` or `confirmed` and the user wants the bar to keep showing it as context. `endless task claim` continues to mean "start working on this task" (changes status to in_progress, creates worktree); `bind` is the lower-impact alternative for display only. Implementation goes through a new `task.bound` event (mirroring `task.released`) so the Go executor handles the sessions DB write per the no-Python-SQLite-writes-in-new-code rule. Use case surfaced 2026-05-11 when E-1240 was in `assumed` and the Claude window working on it could not get the status bar to show the task.

title.current: Convert verbs.json to verbs.jsonl with union merge driver

description.current: Pretty-printed JSON arrays end with ']' on a single line. A defensive check in 'just land' is being filed separately as a recipe fix, since the source design now intentionally allows stale bindings.

title.current: Add merge=union to .gitattributes for .endless/db-ledger/*.jsonl
title.proposed: Add merge=union to .gitattributes for db-ledger files

description.current: The DB ledger files (.endless/db-ledger/db-entries-*.jsonl) are append-only event logs but lack a merge driver in .gitattributes. Concurrent appends on main and a worktree branch produce a 'CONFLICT (content)' on rebase even when both sides only added non-overlapping lines (the worktree branch's lines often turn out to be a subset of main's, since the same events landed in both via parallel auto-record commits). E-1268 already solved this exact problem for verbs.jsonl by adding 'merge=union' in .gitattributes — apply the same pattern to db-ledger/*.jsonl. Same-line duplicates produced by union merge are absorbed at load time by the event reader's natural idempotency on (ts, kind, entity_id). Will eliminate the recurring 'rebase failed on ledger' that has bitten multiple sessions and currently requires the manual 'git checkout main -- .endless/db-ledger/*.jsonl + git rebase --skip' dance.

title.current: Detect already-landed branches in worktree land and message accordingly
title.proposed: Detect already-landed branches in worktree land

description.current: When `endless worktree land E-NNN` runs but E-NNN's worktree is gone, the current error is "No endless-managed worktree for E-NNN" — which implies the work is lost. It isn't; the branch is in main. The worktree is NOT removed by landing: land leaves the directory and branch in place, and the reaper later removes BOTH (`git worktree remove` + `git branch -D`) once the task's task_landings row is older than worktree_ttl (default 14 days), or a human removed it manually (`git worktree remove` / `endless worktree drop`). So a gone worktree is a later condition, not an immediate-after-land one — an immediate multi-session re-land still finds the worktree present and re-lands idempotently. Detect the gone-worktree case and report "E-NNN already landed (commit <sha>); nothing to do" instead of the error — via `git branch --merged main` when the branch survives, or the recorded landing when the branch was reaped too. Fall back to today's error only when the work is genuinely unaccounted for.

Fix: add `--pane` flag to `endless session activity` that overrides TMUX_PANE for session resolution; update the menu item to pass `--pane=#{pane_id}` (tmux substitutes the focused pane at menu invocation, before the popup is spawned). Mirrors the same workaround already used by `endless tmux status-line` and `endless tmux active-id`.

title.current: Add smarter dedup for session_statuses to catch agent-retry near-duplicates within a short window
title.proposed: Add near-duplicate dedup for session_statuses

description.current: Current dedup is strict byte-equal of all content columns against the latest row for the session. Misses the case where an agent retries the same status with slight rewording within seconds — produces two rows that are semantically identical but byte-different. Concrete incident: session 389 rows id=7 and id=8 inserted 2 min apart, same intent, byte-different due to retry-rewording (id=8 deleted as cleanup). Direction options: widen dedup window to a configurable interval; semantic similarity threshold; or refuse near-duplicates and force --amend flow. Discuss at plan time.

title.current: Fix endless session status add hang after successful insert (subprocess fd-closure)
title.proposed: Fix endless session status add hang after insert

description.current: CLI hangs for 1-2+ minutes after the row insert and markdown render complete. Observed: session_statuses row 7 inserted at 20:52:48; the CLI subprocess kept Bash tool in "Channeling" state for 2m15s before manual interrupt. Markdown was already in Bash stdout buffer (visible 46 lines of output) before the hang. Likely culprit: event_bridge.emit_event uses subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True) which blocks on full stdout/stderr drain; if endless-event holds an inherited file descriptor open (Go connection pool, sqlite shutdown, etc.) the Python side waits forever. Investigation: trace endless-event termination after a session_status.recorded emit; check fd table at exit; consider switching event_bridge to Popen with explicit close after a fixed read deadline.

title.current: Clear worktree.lock on task release to keep land's liveness check honest
title.proposed: Clear worktree.lock on task release

description.current: release_item in src/endless/task_cmd.py:2337-2430 emits the task.released event to clear the DB binding but never touches <worktree>/.endless/worktree.lock. The lock file is written at claim time with {pid, session_id, claimed_at}. worktree land's _check_worktree_lock_liveness (src/endless/worktree_cmd.py:185-216) reads the lock file's PID and runs os.kill(pid, 0); if the PID is still alive when land checks (and the original-claiming Claude session often is), land refuses with 'Worktree for E-NNN is owned by a live session' even though the task has been released. Hit during E-1281's land attempt 2026-05-14: release ran cleanly, land kept refusing because the originally-claiming Claude session (PID from claim) was still alive. Workaround was 'rm .endless/worktree.lock' before retry. Fix: release_item should clear (or rewrite to mark released) the lock file as part of its contract, symmetric to claim's lock creation.

title.current: Auto-detect and drop orphan ledger commits during worktree land
title.proposed: Drop orphan ledger commits during worktree land

description.current: Task branches can be left based on Endless: record ledger entry commits that later get superseded on main via the auto-amend flow (canAmend in internal/events/commit.go rewrites a ledger commit's SHA whenever a new event is appended). The orphaned commit then appears as 'in task branch but not on main' and conflicts on rebase, even though main has the equivalent events under a different SHA. Hit on E-1333's land 2026-05-14 (orphan was 0514e4a); resolved manually via git rebase --onto main 0514e4a HEAD. With E-1309's fix preventing NEW rogue commits, this addresses the residual class. Proposal: pre-rebase step in 'endless worktree land' that enumerates commits in task..main with subject==LedgerCommitSubject AND not reachable from main, then drops them via rebase --onto. Cheap to detect, cheap to fix; eliminates manual surgery on every future land that happens to span an amend boundary.

When CLAUDECODE=1 is set in env, refuse --force with a message directing to the legitimate verb for the situation (e.g. 'endless session rebind' for orphaned-session cases, 'endless task bind' for no-status-change cases). Gate, not guardrail: removes the bypass entirely from Claude's reach. Generalize to any --force flag in any endless verb where the legitimate case doesn't apply to a Claude session.

title.current: Add endless session rebind verb for orphaned-but-alive Claude sessions
title.proposed: Add endless session rebind verb for orphaned sessions

description.current: When a Claude session loses its companion file (e.g. via the worktree-delete-on-land cascade addressed by E-1337) but the Claude process is still alive, today there is no legitimate verb to recover. claim --force disclaims the session entirely; task bind has the same missing-companion precondition as claim. Add 'endless session rebind <task-id>' that regenerates the companion file from current TMUX_PANE + CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, writes/revives the sessions row, then performs the same active_task_id bind as task bind. Bypasses the precondition by fixing its upstream cause (missing companion), not by skipping the check. Refuses when CLAUDECODE is not set or TMUX_PANE is unset — the verb's premise is 'recover an alive Claude session'.

title.current: Investigate: SessionStart hook did not re-register Claude session after worktree-delete-on-land
title.proposed: Investigate: SessionStart not re-registering Claude session

description.current: Symptom observed 2026-05-16 during E-1322 verification: after 'endless worktree land 1322' deleted the worktree dir, the original Claude session (uuid 6b597af6...) was marked state=ended in sessions table (correct — SessionEnd hook fired in response to cwd deletion). But the SAME Claude process kept running with a new CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID=bf1f68d3... — and NO new sessions row was inserted for it, NO companion file was written. Either SessionStart hook never fired for the new session ID, or it fired but bailed (perhaps because cwd was deleted at the moment of fire). Downstream of E-1337's root cause but worth focused diagnosis once E-1337 lands — confirms whether E-1337's archive-and-reap fixes this too, or whether a separate SessionStart-on-reincarnate gap remains.

title.current: Add task_followups child table to record post-completion findings without spawning new tasks
title.proposed: Add task_followups table for post-completion findings

description.current: When a bug is found in a task that was recently marked verify/assumed/completed (like E-1322's post-land Kind-guard bug), today the choices are: (a) file a new task per finding, generating process theater; (b) silently append to the original task's outcome, losing the audit trail of when each finding surfaced. A task_followups child table keyed on parent task_id with columns (id, task_id, found_at, found_by_session_id, kind enum {bug, gap, regression, lesson}, notes, status, resolved_at) preserves the audit trail without the per-finding ceremony. Parent task stays in its terminal status; followups have their own lifecycle (open / fixed / wont-fix). Surfaces in task detail under a 'Follow-ups' section. Relates to the parallel decisions-extraction-from-tasks work — both are about making post-creation findings first-class without inflating the primary task list.

title.current: Migrate all schema PRIMARY KEY columns to AUTOINCREMENT to guarantee ID monotonicity
title.proposed: Migrate all PRIMARY KEY columns to AUTOINCREMENT

description.current: All tables currently declare 'id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY' (without AUTOINCREMENT). SQLite reuses deleted IDs in this mode — confirmed 2026-05-17 when E-1403 was reused for a new task immediately after the prior E-1403 was deleted. ID reuse breaks any cross-reference that survives a delete (outcome text, ledger entries, decisions, plan files). Migration: drop+recreate each table preserving data, change column to 'id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT', seed sqlite_sequence with the current max(id). Tables to audit: tasks, sessions, projects, focuses, channels, conversations, messages, notes, task_deps, task_files, session_messages, session_tasks, session_statuses, session_gates, suggestions, activity. E-1344 (soft delete) addresses the same concern via a different lever; both belong long-term — AUTOINCREMENT is belt-and-suspenders for any future hard-purge path.

title.current: Validate ENDLESS_SESSION_ID against the sessions table before trusting it
title.proposed: Validate ENDLESS_SESSION_ID against the sessions table

description.current: The env-var layer of _current_endless_session_id has two defects. (1) It accepts any digit string in ENDLESS_SESSION_ID without checking it matches a sessions-table row, so a bogus or stale value passes the E-1401 gate and misattributes events. (2) The isdigit guard accepts only the integer PK and silently ignores a session UUID, while the gate's remediation message implies any id form works. Survives from obsoleted E-1415 (companion-file portion subsumed by E-1426); defect (2) folded from E-1470. Fix: accept integer PK or UUID (sessions.session_id is UNIQUE), validate against the table, warn and fall through on no match, and align the gate message.

title.current: Fix migrate-db -dry-run silently applying because monitor.DB() auto-migrates on open
title.proposed: Fix migrate-db -dry-run silently applying migrations

description.current: The -dry-run flag on 'endless-event migrate-db' is meaningless on the auto-migrate path. cmd/endless-event main.go calls monitor.DB() to get the connection; DB() unconditionally invokes migrate(db, MigrateOpts{Runner: RunnerAuto}) before main.go reads -dry-run. Fix needs to either split DB-open from auto-migrate, plumb a dry-run signal into DB(), or deprecate the flag as a footgun.

title.current: Fix RequiresRebuild framework gate breaking fresh DBs with no escape hatch
title.proposed: Fix RequiresRebuild migration gate breaking fresh DBs

description.current: When a registered migration sets RequiresRebuild: true, internal/monitor/migrate.go:263 returns ErrRequiresRebuild and refuses to advance the schema unless opts.AllowRebuild is set. There's no way for fresh DBs (tests, new installs) to skip a migration that would be a no-op anyway. Discovered during E-1396 when adding the flag on V11 broke 53 fresh-DB tests immediately, forcing me to drop the flag and rely on BEGIN IMMEDIATE TRANSACTION alone. The flag is currently unused on main but the next user who needs it will hit the same wall — and worse, can't ship it at all without breaking every fresh install. Fix needs an escape hatch: either auto-skip when the rebuild would be a no-op (introspect target shape), or distinguish 'fresh DB created this version' from 'existing DB needs operator approval to rebuild'.

title.current: Use Claude Code env vars as truth for current-pane identification
title.proposed: Use Claude Code env vars to identify the current pane

description.current: After E-1450 lands (hook-fired writes always target the real DB), the dominant cause of attribution failure goes away — the cross-DB sandbox vs real-DB confusion that motivated E-1455's original framing. What remains is detection-side: session_id_resolve() identifies a Claude pane by querying the DB for a matching row, not by reading the env vars Claude Code already exposes (CLAUDECODE=1, CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, TMUX_PANE). This leaves a first-event-timing race (CLI runs before the first hook event has registered the pane in the DB) and unnecessary DB round-trips for current-pane identification. Make env vars the authoritative signal for 'is this a Claude pane and what's its identity'; DB queries remain the mechanism for cross-pane sibling lookup. Composes with E-1450 (does not replace it). Originally framed during E-1396 verification; re-scoped after discovering E-1450 already addresses the cross-DB issue.

title.proposed: Rename worktree_sandbox config key to self_dev

Rename to 'self_dev' because that's the actual semantic — 'this project is endless self-development, so its worktrees should sandbox writes to avoid polluting the real DB.' Scope: rename key in code (config loader, sandbox-init checks), docs (CLAUDE.md mentions worktree DB sandbox), Justfile recipes that reference the flag, and add a one-shot migration that rewrites old worktree_sandbox=true entries to self_dev=true on next config load. The flag is internal/dev-only so a cryptic name is fine; clarity of intent beats consistency with the older terminology.

title.current: Fix collision invalidation that marks live sessions ended on a bare pane-string match

title.current: Fix headless claude -p calls registering pane-owning sessions that false-end the caller
title.proposed: Fix headless claude -p calls ending the caller's session

description.current: Headless claude -p calls (verb-check at task_cmd.py:257; also recap) run subprocess.run with no env scrub, inheriting the caller TMUX_PANE. The headless call gets a new session UUID and fires a hook -> TouchSession(new_uuid, inherited_pane); the collision UPDATE at session.go:271-283 then sets state=ended on the CALLING live session (same pane, different uuid). Repro: a task add titled Adopt spawned the adopt verb-check and ended live session 510; while ended, the resolver (filters state!=ended) cannot resolve the caller, breaking endless session id and task add until the next Stop hook. Recap shares this (session_cmd.py:252 only hides such rows). Fix: scrub TMUX_PANE or set an internal marker in the claude -p env so endless-hook skips session registration+collision for headless calls; also harden the collision rule to confirm the prior pane occupant is actually stale before ending it.

title.current: Make spawn/claim tolerate an orphan task branch instead of failing
title.proposed: Make spawn/claim tolerate an orphan task branch

description.current: When a task's branch (task/<id>-<slug>) exists but its worktree directory is gone (left behind by 'worktree drop' or the reaper, which both keep the branch), create_task_worktree fails on 'git worktree add -b' with 'a branch named X already exists', blocking spawn and claim. Recover instead: if the branch's only delta from main is the plan file, recreate the worktree fresh from main and re-materialize the plan from tasks.text (reconciling DB-vs-file disagreements); if the branch carries real (non-plan) work, error with actionable guidance. Every error must name the problem and hand the user a command or two to resolve it.

title.current: Make schema-mutating endless ops use the worktree's endless-go binary (--db sandbox + Justfile land)
title.proposed: Run schema-mutating ops with the worktree's endless-go

description.current: Two surfaces share one binary-routing gap: schema mutations on a self-dev worktree must run against the worktree's endless-go (which embeds the worktree's schema.sql), but both paths today exec the PATH-resolved global binary at /usr/local/bin/endless-go -> main/bin/endless-go. Main's schema.sql baseline runs, so any additive change the worktree's schema declares is silently absent — leading to 'no such table' errors when subsequent ops (change files, sandbox writes) reference the not-yet-created tables. (a) Python wrapper: when --db sandbox is set and cwd is a self-dev worktree, exec <worktree>/bin/endless-go instead of PATH lookup. (b) Justfile 'land' recipe: PATH-prepend $wt/bin before the 'endless db backup' / 'endless db apply-change' calls so subprocesses inherit the worktree binary. Surfaced 2026-05-29 verifying and then landing E-1378.

title.current: Fix sessions lookup picking ghost rows on reused pane ids after tmux server restart
title.proposed: Fix sessions lookup picking ghost rows on reused pane ids

description.current: internal/monitor/tmux_lookup.go:75 (queryActiveTaskForPanes) joins sessions to tasks on bare 'process' (= tmux pane id) string, orders by last_activity, and returns the top row. Silently assumes tmux pane ids are unique across the DB's lifetime — false when the tmux server restarts (crash, reboot, kill-server, host wake) and the new server reuses pane ids. Stale 'status=active' rows from a previous server win lookups for currently-live panes. Observed: pane %186 in the current server resolves to E-1337 because sessions 482 and 484 (2026-05-21, process='%186', active_task=1337) were never marked ended when their server died. ~9 currently-live panes have ghost rows. Related: E-1468 (false-positive direction — same root cause), E-1173 (Claude UUID as stable identity).
description.proposed: The session lookup by tmux pane id returns stale active rows from a previous tmux server when a restarted server reuses pane ids, so live panes resolve to the wrong task.

title.current: Fix dir-name/task-id mismatch in resolved_worktree_endless_go causing global-binary fallback
title.proposed: Fix worktree endless-go resolution falling back to global

description.current: When endless --db sandbox runs in a self-dev worktree, resolved_worktree_endless_go (src/endless/config.py:333) compares RESOLVED_CONFIG_DIR against sandbox_config_dir(worktree_task_id(cwd)) — passing the digits-only ticket id like '1437' — but apply_db_choice('sandbox') set RESOLVED_CONFIG_DIR = sandbox_config_dir(worktree_dir_name(cwd)) (full name 'e-1437'). The paths never match, the resolver returns None, and event_bridge silently falls back to the global /usr/local/bin/endless-go binary — defeating E-1510's whole purpose. Two latent path-construction sites at the same worktree_task_id callers (f'e-{task_id}') also drop the -slug suffix for slugged worktrees.

title.current: Fix worktree reaper's hard fail on already-deregistered dirs
title.proposed: Fix worktree reaper's hard fail on already-deregistered dirs

description.current: After land, the post-land reaper iterates on-disk worktree dirs and calls 'git worktree remove --force <dir>'. If the dir is no longer tracked by git (e.g. a prior reap removed it from git's admin but didn't rmdir the parent), git returns status 128 with 'is not a working tree' and the reaper aborts loudly on every land. e-1396 is the current trip-wire: empty dir on disk since 2026-06-11, reproduces on each 'just land'. Reaper should treat that error string as a no-op, attempt rmdir to clean up the leftover, and continue; only true failures should surface.

title.current: Investigate verify-suite false greens from swallow-on-failure advisory code

title.current: Reject maybe-phase parent-child relations at task add/update write path
title.proposed: Reject maybe-phase parent-child relations on write

description.current: Add write-path validator that rejects three operations: (1) task add --parent X --phase maybe; (2) task update <maybe-task> --parent X (reparenting a maybe under any parent); (3) task update <child> --phase maybe when child.parent_id IS NOT NULL. Atomic combo task update X --phase next --parent E-Y remains legal (promote+parent in one shot is fine). Rationale: maybe = uncommitted; parent-child = scope binding; mixing creates phantom scope — a parent that appears done while uncommitted commitments linger inside. Hard rejection, no --force (gates not guardrails). Includes a one-shot survey command listing existing pre-rule violations so the owner can convert each to relates_to or leave as standalone. Decision recorded separately.

title.current: Fix worktree land writing task.landed to the sandbox DB when run from a self-dev session
title.proposed: Fix worktree land writing to sandbox DB from self-dev shell

description.current: When `just land` / `endless worktree land` runs from a shell whose XDG_CONFIG_HOME points at a self-dev sandbox (e.g. a Claude session spawned inside a worktree), the land's endless calls inherit that routing and target the SANDBOX DB — but landing is inherently a real/main operation and the landed task lives only in the real DB. The first hard failure is the task.landed emit (task_landings task_id FK 787, seen landing E-1542), but schema-apply/backup are mis-targeted too. Landing should pin the real/main DB regardless of caller routing, like hook/channel/tmux do via PinMainDB (E-1450/E-1429). E-1474 made the emit re-runnable but didn't fix the root cause. Workaround: run land with XDG_CONFIG_HOME set to the real config dir.

title.current: Improve session end so rows close on idle-timeout instead of reaper mass-end sweeps
title.proposed: Improve session end to close rows on idle timeout

description.current: Pattern-B: SessionEnd/EndSession (claude.go:296-298) rarely fires (harness is killed, not cleanly exited), so sessions linger state='working' until a later reaper / collision sweep marks a batch 'ended' at one shared instant (e.g. 6 rows all ending 2026-05-27T02:13:07). Effect: last_activity is bumped far past real life, durations span days, and duration becomes useless as a 'real session' signal. End sessions based on last_activity + idle-timeout (heartbeat staleness) rather than wall-clock sweep time, so end timestamps and durations reflect actual session life.

title.current: Add a submitted status and approve gate to the task status workflow
title.proposed: Add a submitted status and approve gate

description.current: Plan-attach auto-promotes unplanned->ready, so 'ready' means 'agent drafted a plan', not 'Mike approved it' - Mike can't tell reviewed from unreviewed and a background loop can't trust 'ready'. Add a 'submitted' status (replacing the earlier 'unapproved' name): unplanned -> submitted -> (Mike runs approve) ready. 'submitted' = spec-complete, awaiting approval; agent-settable two ways: a plan was attached OR the description alone is a sufficient spec (plan-vs-no-plan carried by tasks.text, not status). This makes unplanned-vs-submitted the spawn-readiness signal (unplanned = needs a plan; submitted = spawnable-from-description, pending approval), so the agent proactively signals which instead of Mike asking. Remove auto-promote; add submit (agent) + approve (Mike) verbs; forbid kind=background sessions from approve and from non-ready pickup.

title.current: Show inherited task/epic in the status row for /bg'd + reattached Claude sessions

description.current: A /bg'd Claude session runs under the Claude daemon with no $TMUX_PANE and a new session id, so endless can't map it to the viewing pane or carry its task/epic across — the status row blanks and never recovers. title.current: Make endless-go hook exit 2 (blocking) on integrity/DB failures so agents halt
title.proposed: Make endless-go hook exit 2 on integrity/DB failures

description.current: The E-1538/E-1571/E-1542 task_types/session_kinds/gate_kinds integrity checks (internal/monitor/db.go:298-330) fail closed, but 'endless-go hook claude' surfaces the failure with a generic non-zero exit, which Claude Code treats as a NON-BLOCKING PostToolUse error: shown to the USER only, never injected into the agent's context (only exit code 2 is fed to the model on PostToolUse). So agents cannot honor 'STOP on errors' for hook/DB failures -- they never see them. DECIDED (Mike): ALWAYS block on integrity failure -- exit 2 from the hook so the agent halts; NO grace window for transient cross-session migration windows (a hard stop while a schema settles is correct and avoids hard-to-unravel ripple effects). Touch-points in analysis.

title.current: Prevent just land's stale-binary record-landing failures
title.proposed: Prevent just land's stale-binary record-landing failures

description.current: E-1660 fixed just land tripping the task_types integrity gate by PATH-prepending the worktree bin to the land call, but binary selection is still a fragile property of the Justfile recipe: each endless-go shellout must individually be pointed at the worktree binary via PATH, and the next one added can silently forget again. Make it deterministic in the land code: _resolve_endless_go() (or land_worktree) should prefer the worktree-built endless-go during a land regardless of --db, since the worktree binary's embedded schema always matches the rows apply-change just inserted. Belt and suspenders: move the apply-change loop out of the Justfile into endless worktree land itself so apply-schema then advance-main then record-landing is one command that always uses the right binary internally, leaving just land a thin build+call+rebuild wrapper.

title.current: Add project-configurable handling for build-regenerated files that dirty the worktree on land
title.proposed: Add project-configurable handling for build-generated files

description.current: Any project with a build system that writes tracked files (tailwind/output.css, templ, codegen, JS bundlers) dirties the worktree when 'worktree land' rebuilds post-merge, which blocks the land or forces recurring manual 'regenerate' commits (output.css hit this 3x in one week). Endless should give a project an elegant, declared way to handle its build-generated artifacts as part of land/build, so it's a one-time configuration rather than an ongoing per-incident chore. General mechanism (e.g. project declares generated paths and/or a regenerate step that land runs+commits or normalizes), NOT an output.css-specific fix.

title.current: Revive a session stuck in 'ended' when its own activity continues
title.proposed: Revive an 'ended' session when its activity continues

description.current: Once a session row is marked 'ended' (by a child /exit, the pane reaper, or collision invalidation), the same session's continued hook activity never revives it: TouchSession's UPDATE branch (session.go:259) deliberately never touches state. Since every reader filters state != 'ended' (E-1530 pane-reuse safety), a still-live session goes permanently invisible — blank tmux status line, 'session next'/nav find nothing, and 'task bind' silently binds onto the dead row. This is the root cause of unreliable session-lifetime tracking. Fix: revive an 'ended' row to a live state when a hook arrives for the same session_id (gated on session_id, not a bare pane match, to preserve E-1530).

title.current: Fix verify-suite assert helpers' silent false-pass when the target isn't executable
title.proposed: Fix assert helpers' false pass when target isn't executable

description.current: The shared verify-script assert_* helpers wrap commands in timeout/gtimeout, which exec a real binary and cannot run a shell convenience function (e.g. go_status). Passing a function yields 'failed to run command' — spurious red on positive checks, and worse a silent GREEN on negative checks (assert_lacks/assert_fails pass whenever the command fails to run at all, regardless of what it would have output). Today the binary-vs-function rule is tribal knowledge with a false-pass failure mode. The framework should make the one correct invocation explicit: own the NO_COLOR/--cols normalization inside the assert helpers (no separate misusable function), OR support functions through the guard (export -f + timeout bash -c), OR hard-error when an assert target isn't executable (type -t check). Surfaced filing E-1689's verify script.

title.current: Fix session monitor not erasing stale line tails on repaint when a new title is shorter
title.proposed: Fix session monitor leaving stale line tails on repaint

description.current: session monitor's live redraw (internal/sessionstatuscmd/session_status.go:238) does '\x1b[H' + frame + '\x1b[J'. The trailing '\x1b[J' erases to end-of-DISPLAY (kills stale ROWS below a now-shorter frame) but does NOT erase each line to end-of-LINE, so when a line's new title is shorter than the prior frame's content on that line, the old tail survives (e.g. E-1461's row keeps E-1698's leftover title text). Fix: erase each line to EOL on repaint - insert '\x1b[K' before each newline in monitorLoop (strings.ReplaceAll(frame, "\n", "\x1b[K\n")) plus one after the last line; keep the trailing '\x1b[J' for the fewer-rows case. Leave the one-shot snapshot renderer free of escapes.

title.current: Reduce transitive over-blocking when a task needs only a trivial sliver of its blocker
title.proposed: Reduce transitive over-blocking on trivial dependencies

description.current: Blocking is task-scoped, but the real dependency is often a sub-scope sliver. Example: E-101 needs only a trivial piece of E-100 (e.g. one new enum value), yet E-100 is itself blocked by a large epic unrelated to E-101 — so E-101 is transitively dragged behind that whole epic when it only needed a one-liner. This delays landings and lets main drift, breeding rebase/integrity conflicts in the waiting worktree. Explore finer-grained options: extract the sliver into its own quickly-landable task, split the blocker, or a dependency that targets just the needed piece and does NOT inherit the blocker's own blockers. title.current: Rebuild the worktree endless-go before land uses it, so a stale binary can't break the landing
title.proposed: Rebuild the worktree endless-go before land uses it

description.current: `just land` runs `endless db apply-change` and `endless worktree land`'s record step using the worktree's bin/endless-go, but only runs `just build` AFTER those steps (the trailing 'Refreshing binaries'). It assumes the worktree binary is already current, and the E-1664 guard only checks it's PRESENT, not CURRENT. So a retained worktree rebased onto a newer main (new schema/enum, e.g. the brainstorm task_type) but not rebuilt lands with a stale binary, which fails the task_types integrity check against the real DB and blocks the landing (hit while closing E-1542). Fix: build the worktree binary up-front, before the apply-change/record steps (or make the E-1664 guard reject a stale binary, not just a missing one). No chicken-and-egg — the up-front build needs nothing the land doesn't already have.

title.current: Broaden canAmend to not amend a ledger commit reachable from any ref besides the current branch
title.proposed: Broaden canAmend to skip commits reachable from other refs

description.current: canAmend (in internal/events/commit.go) coalesces ledger commits by git-amending main's tip, and refuses when the tip is reachable from origin/* (don't rewrite pushed history) — but that guard checks only REMOTE refs, not LOCAL refs based on the same commit. After `worktree land` rebases a worktree branch onto main's tip, the next ledger event amends that tip in place, orphaning the SHA the worktree is based on; taskWorktreeDirty (in internal/monitor/reap_worktrees.go) then falsely reports the worktree '1 ahead'/dirty and re-landing never clears it (wasted session time on E-1542; no data loss — entries are on main). Fix: broaden the guard from 'not reachable from origin/*' to 'not reachable from ANY ref besides the current branch' (incl. worktree branches) — when the tip is shared, append instead of amend. Same rule git enforces against amending a pushed commit, applied to all shared refs.
description.proposed: canAmend amends main's tip ledger commit even when a local worktree branch is based on it, orphaning that SHA; it should amend only when no ref besides the current branch reaches the tip.

title.current: Neutralize committed test-fixture ledger events via the pipeline's revert step
title.proposed: Neutralize committed test-fixture ledger events via revert

description.current: The E-1710 audit found ~36 of 47 committed segment files in main's .endless/db-ledger (~1500 events, ~1/3 of the ledger) are e2e/test-fixture ledgers that create fixture tasks ('smoke epic', 'Coordinate breakdown epic', 'Implement alpha/beta/gamma') reusing real task ids 1..~150. On a full rebuild-db they collide with real ids (UNIQUE conflicts) and corrupt low-id state. Because the ledger is the DB's append-only WAL, the fix is NOT to delete or rewrite the committed segments; instead use the pipeline's revert/tombstone step (E-1720) to append a reversing entry (git-revert-style) that the projector skips at replay, neutralizing the fixture events while preserving history. This task is the first consumer of E-1720. Preventing new pollution is E-1665; rebuild-db robustness to dup/FK is E-1041.

title.current: Make landings survive a rebuild: fix both the projection and the copy-back
title.proposed: Make landings survive a rebuild

description.current: projection(ledger) does not match the live DB for landings, at both ends of the pipeline. BUILD side: the projector fails to insert nearly every task_landings row — (1) it skips session events (projector.go:108), so the temp sessions table is empty and every landing carrying a session_id fails the session_id FK; (2) tasks predating the ledger have no task.created event, so their landings fail the task_id FK. Surfaced by E-1719's historical backfill but affects ALL landings. Which tables belong in the copy-back is for the implementor to settle with the user.

title.current: Isolate sandbox ledger writes so --db sandbox writes db-ledger to the sandbox, not the real project
title.proposed: Isolate sandbox ledger writes from the real project ledger

description.current: The E-1281 sandbox isolates DB writes (--db sandbox / XDG) but NOT ledger writes. emit_event resolves project_root from the projects table (the real checkout) and appends+commits event JSONL to the real .endless/db-ledger/ regardless of --db sandbox. So every sandbox operation — e.g. every 'endless task add --db sandbox' in a tests/tasks/*-verify.sh — permanently writes test-task events (ids 1,2,3... under per-sandbox node ids) into the PRODUCTION ledger, colliding with real E-1..E-96 and making validate-db/rebuild-db noisy. Fix: in sandbox mode route the ledger to a sandbox-local db-ledger dir (mirror the DB isolation), or make sandbox emits DB-only. Surfaced by E-1719's validate-db check. Do this BEFORE the cleanup task, else the leak keeps re-accruing.

title.current: Implement sqlite-vec-backed semantic search (endless search) over tasks and decisions
title.proposed: Implement semantic search over tasks and decisions

description.current: Umbrella for semantic search over the endless ledger using sqlite-vec (in-DB vector KNN). Store an embedding per task/decision (title+description) and answer nearest-neighbor queries sub-millisecond over the 1400+ item ledger, catching paraphrase matches that keyword LIKE misses (e.g. 'Ship endless session id subcommand' vs 'Add endless session id verb'). Powers several consumers: an 'endless search' command, dup-candidate surfacing at task-add time, and relates_to / related-decision suggestions. Open prerequisite Mike is planning: sqlite-vec research — the embedding source must be fast and LOCAL so queries stay sub-second (a network embed adds ~100ms; a full claude -p adds ~10s and is rejected). DB access is being ported to Go (E-1486), so this lands Go-side. Child plans to be filled after the sqlite-vec research. Emerged from the E-1723 brainstorm on search-before-filing.

title.current: Deny task add on semantic-dup matches; override with --ignore-dups=<count>
title.proposed: Deny task add on semantic-duplicate matches

description.current: When 'endless task add' runs, query the sqlite-vec semantic index (E-1738) for existing UNIMPLEMENTED tasks (unplanned/ready/underway/revisit/blocked; skip settled assumed/confirmed/completed/declined/obsolete) similar to the new title+description. If matches exceed the similarity threshold, DENY the add and list them (id, status, title). The agent overrides with --ignore-dups=<num_dups> where the value MUST equal the number of dups found — a bare boolean --ignore-dups is rejected, so Claude cannot habitually bypass the check without reading the findings. Dup detection stays Claude's judgment: similarity surfaces candidates, not verdicts. Depends on E-1738 so task-add stays sub-second (no claude -p at file-time). Converts lesson search-before-filing. title.current: Fix worktree reaper: auto-remove stranded non-empty orphan dirs and stop false 'removed' logging
title.proposed: Fix worktree reaper leaving stranded orphan dirs

description.current: The worktree reaper logs 'removed <dir>' for stranded orphan worktree dirs (non-empty, no .git, untracked by git) on every sweep, yet never deletes them: 'git worktree remove' fails with 'is not a working tree', the os.Remove fallback refuses the non-empty dir, its error is discarded, and the function returns reaped=true anyway — so the log lies and the dirs persist forever. Fix: auto-remove stranded orphans via a strictly path-scoped RemoveAll (only <main>/.endless/worktrees/e-NNN, non-symlink) and surface genuine removal failures instead of faking success.

title.current: Add a handoff-status command that reports only out-of-band git anomalies
title.proposed: Add a handoff-status command reporting only git anomalies

description.current: On session handoff the agent narrates git side-effects (uncommitted files, stray tags, unlanded commits, leaked worktrees, working-tree cleanliness). Because the spawn prompt enumerates these as categories to report, a clean repo yields 'nothing to report' dressed as reporting — pure noise. Provide a command that inspects the repo itself and prints ONLY non-empty findings; a clean state prints nothing. The agent's final message then reduces to what it genuinely can't compute: how-to-verify and the return line. This moves the 'is clean worth saying?' judgment out of the agent (which errs toward self-covering) into a tool where empty output IS the representation of clean — the durable fix for this class of noise.

title.current: Add --ascii flag to `session status` for copy-safe single-byte text output
title.proposed: Add --ascii flag to `session status` for copy-safe output

description.current: `endless session status` (the endless-go session-status renderer) is a display view that leads each row with a ✎ pencil glyph (U+270E) and truncates titles with a … ellipsis (U+2026), plus tree/box-drawing glyphs. Those multibyte UTF-8 chars garble when the output is copied as plain text through editors (observed: pasting via pbcopy→nano made task IDs look wrong and they got hand-corrupted). Add an --ascii flag that substitutes every decorative multibyte glyph with a single-byte ASCII equivalent (e.g. pencil→*, ellipsis→..., tree glyphs→|/+/-), so the view is usable as copy-safe text. Default output is unchanged; --ascii is opt-in. Task IDs are already plain ASCII, so only the decoration needs transliterating.

title.current: Add `endless session resume <ref>` to relaunch a lost Claude session in the current pane
title.proposed: Add `endless session resume <ref>` for lost Claude sessions

description.current: Adds `endless session resume <ref>` to relaunch a Claude session orphaned when tmux crashes — the pane processes die, but the session transcripts and ledger rows survive. Resolves <ref> (a task id as shown on the tmux tab, a session id, or a Claude UUID prefix) to the session's UUID and its task worktree, cd's into the worktree, and execs `claude --resume <uuid>` so the resumed session takes over the current pane. Resolution is task-first and, unlike `session goto`, includes ended sessions, since a crash takes every session to a dead pane. The task->session lookup runs in Go via a `session-query resume-target` verb (no new Python SQLite reads).

title.current: Derive test regression by diffing runs against the last-green baseline
title.proposed: Derive test regression from the last-green baseline

description.current: Split out of E-1771. Determine whether a failing test is a regression (passed on a prior commit, now broken) versus never-worked — computed by diffing a run against the last-green baseline in captured test history, NOT asserted by the agent (a single session lacks a trustworthy baseline; asking it to classify invites 'probably not my fault' self-cover). Frame the result as a recoverability signal — 'this test has a known-green ancestor, so a working version exists in VCS' — not blame; most meaningful at project scope. Blocked by E-1777: regression can only be derived once test-run history is captured as structured rows.

title.current: Replace less with a pannable terminal viewer so wide tables stay readable
title.proposed: Replace less with a pannable terminal viewer

description.current: E-1775 makes markdown tables always fit the screen width and rely on vertical scroll, because less -R wraps any over-width line into an unreadable mess (it only pans on manual arrow-chop, and launching with -S would also chop the soft-wrapped prose). That is a stopgap: a genuinely wide table gets squeezed into narrow, tall columns with no way to see the full-width layout. The long-term fix is to replace the external less pager (spawned from task_cmd for -p) with a self-contained terminal viewer supporting smooth horizontal panning plus vertical scroll, so a table can render at natural width and the user pans left-right (columns sliding, not replaced). Mike's go-tealeaves teagrid (a BubbleTea grid pager) is prior art and a likely basis; this also drops the external less dependency (the E-1746 deferred note). Scope to settle when planned: general pager vs table-aware grid, less fallback, pan interaction model.

title.current: Suppress agent plan-recap prose when a plan is written
title.proposed: Suppress agent plan-recap prose when a plan is written

description.current: After an agent writes a plan (endless task update --text, or plan-mode save), the chat re-narrates the plan's contents to the user, forcing them to review the same material twice (the plan AND the recap). Same disease as end-of-session ceremony: restating a reviewable artifact. Fix on E-1772's mechanism: task update --text emits a stdout reminder that the plan is saved and must NOT be recapped; the agent replies only with a genuine open decision or blocker needing an answer before implementing (the 'one thing worth your eye' paragraph), or nothing. Reminder wording tunable via the report-prompts.jsonl surface.

title.current: Sandbox snapshot/restore: save and restore a sandbox to named point-in-time copies
title.proposed: Save and restore sandboxes as named snapshots

description.current: A general Endless sandbox capability to save a sandbox's state to a named point-in-time snapshot and restore it on demand (a cheap dir/DB copy; the existing 'event backup' VACUUM-INTO is a starting point). Motivated by the verify system: a verify run resets the worktree's canonical sandbox to a known state at run start (E-1608), and snapshotting lets the agent optionally preserve and later restore the pre-verify sandbox state instead of maintaining a second sandbox. It is an opt-in choice specified in verify.toml (stubbed on the verify side for now), so the common path stays cheap; retention/pruning bounds storage. General-purpose beyond verify.

Replace the translate/capture struct-of-funcs registry (internal/verify/check.go firstClassRunners) with a RunnerDriver Go interface: each driver EXECUTES its run (os/exec, capture stream, normalize to CTRF-subset) rather than returning a command string. gotest and pytest become drivers. Add the pytest/uv registered variant with contract-defined launcher resolution (prefer project venv plain pytest executable that survives HOME-isolation, then uv run pytest, then bare pytest); bare pytest keeps documented fallback precedence. A generic driver covers raw/shell/arbitrary-tool runners: exec the declared command, require a normalizable result stream (TAP/CTRF). Unblocks E-1605's pytest slice. See E-1789 outcome for the full design.

title.proposed: Path gate blocks relative-path tokens as if absolute

description.current: The inline-content path gate rejects tokens that are not absolute paths, reporting them as absolute. Two observed cases: a relative-path-form token like pytest/uv (a runner type/subtype, intended to be allowed), and a bare/standalone slash such as '/' used as an illustrative delimiter in prose.
