title.current: Document the in-session follow-up loop and slice-extraction unblock practices in the guide
title.proposed: Document follow-up loop and slice-extraction practices

description.current: Capture two hard-won Endless workflow practices in the session guide (docs/guide), agent-first but human-usable. (1) A session does not stop at its bound task's implementation — it closes the discovery loop: walk session status, chase blockers, file+plan follow-ups. Document in the happy path as the reconciliation with one-worktree-per-task so agents don't over-index on 'one session == one task' and wrongly tell users to stop. (2) Don't passively accept a block: if the dependent needs only a small independent slice of the blocker, extract that slice and link relates_to instead of blocked_by. Guide-only; the README restructure and the link-command over-blocking gates are separate tasks.

title.current: Extend task report to gate every in-session user-facing checkpoint, not just session end
title.proposed: Extend task report to every in-session user checkpoint

description.current: Two coupled facets of one goal — cut agent review-burden via task report. (1) COVERAGE: make task report the mandated channel at ALL in-session user-facing checkpoints (not just session end/status); acceptable output defined FUNCTIONALLY — a computed fact the user can't derive XOR a genuine open decision, else nothing (report's notes vs questions), not an enumerated list (drifts). (2) ENFORCEMENT: add a PostToolUse hook matched to the task report Bash invocation that injects hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext telling the agent to relay the report output verbatim and add nothing — a contextual, compose-time, harness-authoritative nudge. Honest limit (see analysis): Claude Code can't make the tool output BE the agent's message, so this is the strongest in-harness lever short of a regenerate loop — a strong nudge, not a hard gate.

title.current: Explore a task complexity field (0–5) to drive handoff review depth
title.proposed: Explore a task complexity field for handoff review depth

description.current: Idea from Mike, sparked by Matt Pocock's video 'Do you even need a human review?'. Add a tasks.complexity field valued 1..5 where 1 is trivial, 5 is highly complex, and 0 means not-yet-evaluated. The payoff: handoff documents and prompts could adapt their approach based on complexity. Concretely, shift the human-review checkpoint LEFT for complex work (align heavily up front, since late fixes are expensive) and RIGHT for simple work (single-prompt, ship, review only at the end). Brainstorm the field, its scale semantics, who or what sets it, and how handoffs plus the review workflow would consume it.

title.proposed: Refactor tmux operations behind a multiplexer driver

Builds on the endless-go launch seam introduced when spawn moved to CLI-arg prompt delivery: that change put the in-window launch behind endless-go, but Python still triggers window creation and passes tmux-specific params. This task moves the remaining tmux knowledge behind the driver so no caller shells out to tmux directly.

title.proposed: Decouple Endless session launch and drive from tmux

description.current: Umbrella initiative to make Endless multiplexer-agnostic and rethink how agent sessions are launched and driven. Today tmux is hard-wired: window creation, window-option plumbing, session launch/attach, and pane->session/task resolution all shell out to tmux directly from both the Go binaries and the Python CLI. Goal: route every multiplexer operation through a driver interface with pluggable backends (tmux now; Herdr https://herdr.dev/; a multiplexer built into Endless itself), and remove the fragile send-keys keystroke-injection path entirely. Children cover the exploration (brainstorm), the foundational launch-seam step, and the full driver refactor.

title.current: Deliver a task's type handoff on claim-into-a-live-session, not only on spawn

Not under E-1785 (output discipline) -- a context-delivery gap.

title.current: Require surfaced facts to be verified against live state, not inferred or recalled
title.proposed: Require surfaced facts to be verified against live state

description.current: E-1803's report-channel gate ('surface a computed fact the user can't derive XOR a genuine open decision, else nothing') assumes the surfaced fact is TRUE. The costliest agent outputs are confidently-wrong facts the user must track down to disprove -- worse than ceremony. Add a veracity requirement: any surfaced computed fact must be verified against live state (git, the ledger, the file) at the moment of surfacing, never inferred or recalled from earlier context; a wrong fact must clear a HIGHER bar than an omitted one. Some classes are mechanically catchable and worth a lightweight check: an agent-authored task-ID citation whose target doesn't resolve or is topically unrelated, or a state claim git contradicts. Distinct from E-1803, which governs output VOLUME; this governs output VERACITY.

title.current: Record task report checkpoints and surface report-channel compliance in session monitor
title.proposed: Record report checkpoints and show them in session monitor

description.current: Complements E-1803's enforcement arm by making report-channel compliance observable, since the nudge is unenforceable. (1) 'task report' records a checkpoint event (session, task, timestamp) to the ledger on each call -- durable, not ephemeral stderr. (2) 'session monitor' surfaces per-session last-checkpoint ('last checkpoint: 2m ago', with a separator line) so a glance shows which sessions are reporting. (3) A Stop hook that only RECORDS turn-end (returns success, never blocks -- so no regenerate, sidestepping the Stop-hook-as-gate E-1803 rejected) lets the monitor show turns-or-time since last report, making a MISSED checkpoint visible. Detection logic baked into endless code, not settings.json config.

title.current: Harden verb registration: strip title punctuation and reject duplicate verbs
title.proposed: Harden verb registration against punctuation and duplicates

description.current: Two interlocking hygiene bugs on the verb-registration write path, shared by both auto-registration (a title's first word) and manual endless verb add. (1) Auto-registration registers a punctuated/uppercase token verbatim: filing 'Create, publish, and maintain a ROADMAP for Endless' registered the verb 'create,' (with the comma) instead of 'create'. Extraction should strip trailing punctuation and lowercase before registering. (2) The add path accepts a value that already exists in the resolved registry (project > machine > defaults), appending a duplicate line to .endless/verbs.jsonl instead of erroring; it should refuse with a clear error naming the existing verb (case-insensitive), leaving the registry unchanged. The two interlock: once (1) normalizes 'create,' to 'create', the (2) dedup guard is what prevents re-adding the already-registered 'create'. Also clean up the existing 'create,' junk verb. Discovered while filing E-1834 and reviewing verbs.jsonl during E-1833.

title.current: Fix verb gate treating classifier failure as NO and losing valid verbs
title.proposed: Fix verb gate treating classifier failure as NO

Replace the boolean check with a named-outcome result that distinguishes the failure modes, retries the transient ones, and offers reword only on a definitive NO. See analysis for the full outcome taxonomy and retry policy.

Runs as belt (inline at file time) and suspenders (background sweep over the untriaged queue).

title.current: Add a way to revert a decision from accepted or rejected back to proposed
title.proposed: Add a way to revert a settled decision to proposed

description.current: Make a settled decision reversible. Before this, 'decision accept' and 'decision reject' were one-way: 'decision update' has no --status flag and no reverse verb existed, so an accidental accept was permanent. Ships three verbs: 'decision unaccept' (accepted to proposed, guarded on 'accepted'), 'decision unreject' (rejected to proposed, guarded on 'rejected', and clears the stored rejection_reason), and 'decision reconsider' (dispatches to whichever applies, unguarded). Deliberately NOT named 'reopen': a decision is proposed and then accepted or rejected, so it is never 'open'. The guarded pair is the primary surface because each verb asserts the status you believe you are in, so aiming one at the wrong terminal status errors instead of silently performing the other reversal. Immediate need: ED-1517 was accidentally accepted and must be reverted so it can then be rejected or superseded per E-1863.

title.current: Show creating session on task show Created: line, plus a Touched by: session list
title.proposed: Show creating and touching sessions on task show

description.current: `task show` never reveals which session/active task created a task, nor which others touched it, so there is no path from a task back to the sessions that worked it -- and therefore no way to know what to pass to `session goto`. Add the creating session (and its active task) to the `Created:` line, and add a `Touched by:` section listing every session that touched the task, laid out like the existing `This task:` relations block so it reads as a peer. Each entry should carry enough identity (session id + its active task) to feed `session goto` directly. Surfacing these makes a task a navigational hub for jumping between the sessions that shaped it.

title.current: Fix session status showing ordinary done tasks as ⁇ unknown under --all
title.proposed: Fix session status showing done tasks as ⁇ unknown

description.current: Under `endless session status --all`, an ordinary done task renders with ⁇ — the renderer's should-never-happen glyph — and the legend then advertises '⁇ unknown', so a perfectly normal row reads as a bug in the tool. Cause: classify() (internal/sessionstatuscmd/session_status.go) has no case for the five terminal statuses (confirmed/assumed/declined/obsolete/completed), so any terminal row that is not focal/parent/from/in-flight and has never landed falls through to default → actUnknown. declined and obsolete tasks never land by definition, so they are ALWAYS ⁇. See the analysis for the reproduction, the classification decisions the fix needs, and an adjacent stale comment to fix with it.

title.current: Add task annotate as the agent's write-only observation sink, hidden by default
title.proposed: Add task annotate as a write-only observation sink

description.current: Agents narrate discharged facts into chat partly because displaced observations have no destination. Project notes are not that destination -- they are project-scoped, have found no good use since being added, and are likely to be deprecated. Add `endless task annotate <id> "..."`: task-scoped, append-only, write-only by design, and hidden from the default `task show` -- surfaced only under `task show --annotations`, so the sink never relocates noise to where the user already reads. This is the CAPTURE half of a pair; E-1803 owns ENFORCEMENT (task report as the mandated channel plus a PostToolUse nudge). Neither half works alone: a sink without the gate yields annotate-and-narrate, giving the user a third place to read, while the gate without a sink forces the agent to either drop genuine observations or smuggle them into prose. E-1865 is the evidence that a destination alone is insufficient -- every fact narrated there already had a durable home.

description.current: One job, one pass per worktree, two steps in a fixed order. Step 1, the original scope: sync endless-auto commits touching only .endless/plans, .endless/analyses and .endless/db-ledger from each worktree branch up to main — never code or tests, which stay gated by the normal land workflow. title.current: Add endless worktree reconcile to resolve stale endless-managed commits
title.proposed: Add endless worktree reconcile for stale managed commits

description.current: Detects and resolves the scenario where a long-lived worktree accumulates endless-generated commits (plan/analysis/ledger updates) that overlap or are superseded by main's independent updates, causing 'just land' to hit rebase conflicts. Classifies each unlanded commit by files touched: (a) endless-managed metadata (.endless/plans, .endless/analyses, .endless/db-ledger) that match or are superseded on main → safe to drop, (b) endless-managed metadata with genuinely unique branch content → preserve with clear per-file explanation, (c) any non-endless-managed file → bail out (real work that needs land, not reconcile). Output should tell the operator exactly what would happen before doing anything destructive. Invocable standalone as 'endless worktree reconcile <id>' or as a --reconcile fallback flag on 'endless worktree land'. title.current: Record a fault when a Claude hook's database write fails

description.current: A hook that cannot write to the database reports it to nobody. monitor.TouchSession is the writer behind sessions.process_id — the single value the tmux status line resolves a pane through — and it runs on every hook event. When it fails, hook.Run log.Printf's the error and exits 0, deliberately, so a broken hook never blocks a tool call. Claude discards that stderr, so the only symptom is a blank status bar, which is also what a pane with no task looks like. Session ES-1055 ran that way for four weeks: every PreToolUse died with 'table sessions has no column named process', process_id stayed NULL, and nothing anywhere recorded it. Record a fault instead, so the failure lands in the fault row session status already renders. The read half of this — faults.Record in runStatusLine — shipped inside E-1898 and is not in scope; a read-side recorder could not have caught this, because the read returned no error. It correctly found no session, because the write never happened.

title.current: Consolidate the task status vocabulary behind one Go accessor
title.proposed: Consolidate task status vocabulary behind one Go accessor

description.current: Status is the only vocabulary in the system with no owning package — task type, session kind, and session-task relation each have one, and tasktype even carries String()/Label(). Status is bare string literals across ~15 sites in two languages: whole-vocabulary copies, policy subsets, lists embedded in SQL string literals, and per-status glyph/label/derivation ordering. The failure mode is omission, not typos: E-1648 added 'submitted' and missed two sites (both still broken today), and E-1845 had to hand-edit every site for 'untriaged' with nothing to catch a miss. Fix: one Go package owning every grouping in a single map, with Get/Has/SQLList/Rank/Label/Glyph accessors, exposed as one CLI subcommand per function; Python wrappers are pure pass-through and hold no knowledge of the registry's structure. Absorbs E-1888.

title.current: Fix --keep-status so it suppresses the plan-attach promotion too
title.proposed: Fix --keep-status to suppress plan-attach promotion

description.current: `--keep-status` does not suppress the plan-attach promotion: attaching plan text to an `untriaged`/`unplanned` task moves it to `submitted` even when the flag is passed. The promotion lives in the Go executor (`execTaskFieldsUpdated`), gated only on "the caller set status explicitly", while `--keep-status` is a Python-side flag guarding only the E-1762 auto-revisit and the E-1845 auto-untriage. title.current: Block line numbers and other time-frozen specifics from durable task content
title.proposed: Block time-frozen specifics from durable task content

description.current: ED-1073 already forbids time-frozen specifics — byte counts, file sizes, line numbers, sha hashes — and says to cite file or function names instead so the reader re-locates at pickup. It is violated routinely because nothing enforces it and two things undercut it: ED-1073's own text scopes the rule to the analysis field, so a literal reading does not reach a plan in text, a description, or an outcome; and the tasks guide describes text as a full implementation plan 'including approach, file paths, verification steps', which invites the thing the decision forbids. Three parts: extend the content gate that already refuses absolute paths in --description/--text so it also refuses file.ext:NNN and bare :NNN citations; widen ED-1073 to govern all durable content; and fix the guide's wording to say file and function names. Prompted by E-1929's plan, which cited line numbers throughout and goes stale as soon as anything else lands.

title.current: Make db-ledger rebuild reliable enough to trust over the main DB
title.proposed: Make db-ledger rebuild trustworthy over the main DB

description.current: Today the main DB is canonical and rebuild-db is not trusted: a rebuild is neither robust nor reliable, so it must not be exercised against real data, and verify scripts have to route around it. That is a load-bearing gap — the ledger is supposed to be the source of truth the DB projects from, and E-1829's two-developer milestone depends on each developer rebuilding the projection from the shared ledger. Until rebuild is trustworthy, every executor handler has a projector twin that nothing exercises end to end, so divergence between them is invisible until someone rebuilds and loses data. Umbrella for the work that closes that gap: existing candidates include E-1671 and E-1674 (event upcasting so old events replay into the current schema), E-1728 (projector failing task_landings inserts), E-1716 (committed test-fixture ledger events), E-1883 (DB scoping so a rebuild is project-safe), and executor/projector parity testing in general. Relate or reparent those once the shape is agreed.

title.current: Derive epic status from children instead of storing it by hand
title.proposed: Derive epic status from children

description.current: Epic status is intended to be a rollup of child statuses but no rollup logic exists anywhere: epic_cmd.py is a thin wrapper over the task commands (add/list/show/update), and an epic's status is a plain stored column set by hand like any other task's. Consequence: an epic whose children are all terminal keeps whatever status was last written, so the ledger asserts work is underway when nothing is. Surfaced when every child of a parent was obsoleted and the parent stayed underway. Decide the derivation rule (what child statuses produce which parent status, how mixed sets resolve, whether a hand-set status can override) and whether it computes on read or on child mutation. Note the parent in question was typed todo rather than epic, so also decide whether derivation keys on type=epic or on has-children.

title.current: Rework just land's ordering so no failure can leave the DB ahead of the code
title.proposed: Rework just land's ordering so the DB never leads the code

description.current: Landing E-1898 on 2026-08-10 produced two failures in the land recipe itself. First, `just land` rebuilds the worktree binary but never checks the worktree's SOURCE is current with main, so a branch 147 commits behind rebuilt a still-stale binary and aborted on an unrelated enum-drift error naming gate_kinds. Second — and the expensive one — apply-change then SUCCEEDED and the merge failed, leaving the real database migrated to a schema no installed binary understood; session tracking froze machine-wide and recovery needed a manual restore. The justfile only reasons about apply FAILING ("the land aborts before main advances"); apply succeeding and the merge failing is the unhandled, irreversible case. Fix: refuse the land when the branch is behind main, rehearse the merge on a throwaway branch, fast-forward main to that result, and apply schema changes AFTER the merge so a failed apply is merely a retry. Analysis carries the full sequence.
description.proposed: `just land` can apply schema changes and then fail the merge, leaving the database migrated ahead of any installed binary; reorder it so no failure leaves the DB ahead of the code.

segments.text: Landing E-1898 on 2026-08-10 produced two failures in the land recipe itself.

First, `just land` rebuilds the worktree binary but never checks the worktree's SOURCE is current with main, so a branch 147 commits behind rebuilt a still-stale binary and aborted on an unrelated enum-drift error naming gate_kinds. Second — and the expensive one — apply-change then SUCCEEDED and the merge failed, leaving the real database migrated to a schema no installed binary understood; session tracking froze machine-wide and recovery needed a manual restore.
The justfile only reasons about apply FAILING ("the land aborts before main advances"); apply succeeding and the merge failing is the unhandled, irreversible case.

Fix: refuse the land when the branch is behind main, rehearse the merge on a throwaway branch, fast-forward main to that result, and apply schema changes AFTER the merge so a failed apply is merely a retry.
Analysis carries the full sequence.

title.current: Add endless db restore to recover from a backup safely
title.proposed: Add endless db restore to recover from a backup safely

description.current: `endless db backup` exists and `just land` calls it, but there is no way to USE a backup — recovery is an unguided `cp`. On 2026-08-10 that went wrong twice: copying over a database with six open connections left a hot journal that made every reader fail with 'database is locked', and `VACUUM INTO` backups are rollback-journal while the live DB is WAL, so connections then fought over switching it back. Add `endless db restore [<backup>]` that defaults to the newest backup, REPORTS open connections by pid/command rather than killing them silently, keeps the pre-restore file aside, and afterwards re-establishes WAL and runs `PRAGMA integrity_check` failing loudly on anything but 'ok'. A dry-run mode printing holders and journal mode is what you actually want mid-incident.

title.current: Decide how worktree branches survive a rewrite of main's history
title.proposed: Decide how worktree branches survive a rewrite of main

description.current: Worktree branches lose their base when main's history is rewritten under them — not from amending. canAmend already refuses to amend a tip another ref can reach, but implements that as SHA reachability, so once `git pull --rebase` rewrites main the guard answers a question the rewrite made meaningless, permits the amend, and the land rebase then conflicts on the append-only ledger segment. Endless must work under either `pull.rebase` setting: rebase-style pull is mainstream, and a guard that silently degrades under it is a defect regardless of which setting this repo uses. Decide how — give a fork point an identity that survives a rewrite, keep rewrites away from ledger commits, or detect the condition before rebasing and refuse with a named diagnosis. Any SHA-reachability-based fix inherits the same blindness; the union-merge-driver option is struck (it would corrupt the ledger). Analysis carries the evidence. Deliverable is a decision plus follow-on tasks.

title.current: Decide who may define, migrate, and use the DB schema, and when
title.proposed: Decide who may define, migrate, and use the DB schema

description.current: The 2026-08-10 incident produced four distinct failures from one question. `monitor.DB()` applies schema.sql on EVERY connection, so any binary additively migrates whatever DB it opens; E-1818's schema-passive mode stops that for pinned surfaces but only protects the DB from the binary, never the binary from the DB — a candidate binary against a main-schema ledger (or vice versa) passes connect cleanly and then fails at runtime writing or reading columns that aren't there. title.current: Make status routing read as the agent's job at every point of occurrence
title.proposed: Make status routing read as the agent's job

description.current: Agents repeatedly narrate 'this sends it back through triage' after a description edit, treating the reset as a system outcome to route around rather than a routing call to make. Three things teach that. CLAUDE.md documents triage running automatically, which reads as exclusivity — the mechanism gives an agent nothing actionable and invites deferral. task update's transition message offers only --keep-status to suppress, never naming the decision. And task update --status rejects 'submitted', so the one-call path exists for 'needs a plan' but not for 'the description is sufficient', making the right answer the harder one to reach. Fix all three: accept submitted in --status (task submit stays as the standalone verb), reword the transition message to lead with DECIDE YOURSELF and name the background sweep as a worst-case fallback, and drop the automation mechanics from CLAUDE.md — agents need the duty, not the machinery.

title.current: Explore how a self-dev session reports Endless blocking it instead of working around it
title.proposed: Explore how a self-dev session reports Endless blocking it

description.current: When an agent using Endless hits something that should work but does not, the reflex is to work around it silently and keep going — the user never learns the product blocked them. Observed this session: task update --status rejected submitted, and the workaround (a second task submit call) was applied without comment until asked. In self_dev mode especially the agent is a user of the product, and its friction is product signal. Reporting means TELLING THE USER IN CHAT, not filing a task — auto-filing would raise the file-to-close ratio this is partly meant to protect. Decide: what counts as blocked-but-should-work versus an ordinary error, how the agent phrases it inline without derailing the task at hand, how to keep it from becoming noise, and whether it applies only under self_dev or to any project.

title.current: Decide how per-worktree sandboxes become available to all projects, not just self_dev
title.proposed: Decide how per-worktree sandboxes reach all projects

description.current: Sandbox provisioning is gated on `self_dev: true`, so only Endless itself gets per-worktree sandboxes: `_maybe_auto_sandbox_bind` (worktree_cmd.py) returns early for other projects and `config.py` resolves the sandbox root to None for them. That gate was never an intended design decision — the intent was that EVERY project gets a sandbox, because a sandbox is where a worktree stores the configuration a task needs in order to be verified, and essentially no real software project has zero configuration files. What is genuinely Endless-specific is only the `endless.db` routing (downstream worktree tasks must still land in the real ledger as real audit data, not a throwaway copy). title.current: Make the session and task movement verbs account for task state
title.proposed: Make session/task movement verbs account for task state

description.current: One root behind four defects: the verbs that move between sessions and tasks act on task state without making it explicit. `task reopen` releases a session's binding silently (its help says 'no session binding', which reads as 'does not create one'). `session resume` clobbers the current pane even when that pane holds live work. `session goto --resume` cannot express intent about a task needing revisit. And `task spawn --reopen` exists only because none of the navigation verbs could change status. Fix together: `--force` plus an unsuppressible announcement on reopen's release; `--force` on resume when the current pane holds a task; `--revisit`/`--no-revisit` on `session goto --resume`; retire `task spawn --reopen`; and rewrite spawn's done-ish refusal, which currently offers 'run task reopen first' as one of two routes — the one that dismantles the guard that produced the message.

title.current: Surface the triager's decision and rationale so a no-op routing is visible
title.proposed: Surface the triager's decision and rationale

description.current: Triage records its call as a task.status_changed event with actor.kind=triager, carrying the deciding model and a one-line rationale in the payload. Nothing reads it. task show displays neither, so a triage decision that lands on unplanned is indistinguishable from a task that was never triaged. This caused a live misdiagnosis on 2026-08-08: E-1847, E-1891 and E-1893 were manually set to untriaged, the sweep judged all three and routed each back to unplanned with a specific, correct rationale, and the feature was reported as not working because the end state matched the start state. E-1859's plan called that payload 'what you want when triage starts making calls you disagree with' but never gave it a reader. Surface it: at minimum the rationale and when it was triaged, on task show. Consider making 'triaged, verdict unplanned' read differently from 'never triaged' wherever untriaged/unplanned are rendered, since that distinction is the whole point of the untriaged status.

title.current: Fix ledger auto-commit failing when a concurrent writer holds the git index lock
title.proposed: Fix ledger auto-commit failing on a held git index lock

description.current: Every event emit runs git add plus git commit --amend on the project's main checkout, because E-1309 routes all ledger commits there — making that one repo a shared write point for every concurrent worktree session, the triage sweep, and any foreground command. The commit takes .git/index.lock with no retry, so when two writers overlap the endless command fails with git's raw 'another git process seems to be running' text and its DB write is lost. Fix in the Go commit path: retry lock acquisition with backoff, or coalesce appends so one commit covers a burst instead of one commit per event.

title.current: Decide how Claude hooks should choose between main's and a worktree's endless-go
title.proposed: Decide which endless-go binary Claude hooks invoke

description.current: A worktree's `.claude/settings.json` pins every Claude hook to that worktree's own `bin/endless-go` (E-998, so spawned sessions test candidate hook code). When that binary is stale it aborts before doing anything — a Jul 29 build dies on the E-1659 `task`→`todo` integrity check — so SessionStart never registers the session and the Claude window runs completely untracked, with the error on hook stderr nobody reads. Measured today: 135 worktrees, 89 pinned to their own binary, and all 103 existing worktree binaries older than main's. Invert it: hooks always invoke main's known-good binary, which delegates to the worktree's only when that binary is verified compatible, so a stale or missing one becomes a warning from a working process instead of a dead session.

title.current: Fix session_liveness multiplying rows for panes in linked tmux windows
title.proposed: Fix session_liveness multiplying rows for linked tmux panes

description.current: Regression from E-1898, found hours after land. `tmux list-panes -a` lists a LINKED window's panes once per tmux session the window is linked into (measured: 442 rows for 245 distinct panes, every pane twice). `refreshLiveness` inserts one `live_processes` row per returned pane and that TEMP table has no uniqueness constraint, so `session_liveness`'s LEFT JOIN multiplies each session's row and every consumer inherits it — `list-live` returns 114 rows for 57 sessions and `esu` refuses with 'Multiple sibling Claude panes in this window', blocking worktree entry by session. Fix: give `live_processes` the same expression-based unique index the durable `processes_identity` already uses, insert with OR IGNORE, and do the same for `observed_servers`. Regression test must INSERT a duplicate address directly — `SetTestTmuxObservation` builds panes from a Go map and cannot express one, which is why no existing test caught this.

title.current: Build the minimizer autoresearch loop with a judge-scored, user-calibrated optimizer
title.proposed: Build the minimizer autoresearch loop

description.current: Replace the shipped deletion-only minimizer with one that rewrites and deduplicates against what the user already has (ED-1557), and wrap it in an automated optimization loop the user never gates (ED-1556). The user supplies ground truth in the flow of work via free-form span-scoped labels (ED-1555) and picks between paired A/B minimizations; an LLM judge scores every turn and is calibrated by blind prediction against those reactions. The optimizer generates variants — seeded from controlled-English grammars — and jointly tunes prompt text, a JSON fetch policy, and the bypass threshold, split by task type. Promotion is decided by paired replay over a frozen corpus with invariant vetoes, never by a weighted average or a rolling mean. Rides the existing job runner. Full design in --analysis; E-1953's viewer-contingent decisions lapse.

title.current: Judge worktree settledness by content reachability, not commit SHA
title.proposed: Judge worktree settledness by content, not commit SHA

description.current: `session status`, `task unsettled` and `worktree drop` judge settledness by commit SHA, so a worktree whose work is fully in main reports UNLANDED forever after a rebasing land — `land` rewrites every commit under a new SHA and the branch keeps the originals. The verdict is not merely noisy, it is inverted: a permanent red light on a settled worktree trains the operator to ignore the one signal that must be trusted, and `task unsettled` then advises `worktree land`, which is the wrong and potentially destructive action. Fix by judging content, not SHA: for each differing path ask whether the branch's blob is reachable anywhere in main's history for that path (stale) or not (genuinely unique); paths absent on the branch just mean main is newer. Fix the probe itself so every consumer inherits it. A reaper pass or `worktree reconcile` (E-1882) is a separate remedy and cannot substitute for a correct verdict.

title.current: Add endless worktree reset to converge a diverged-but-superseded worktree
title.proposed: Add endless worktree reset

description.current: Add `endless worktree reset <id>` to converge a worktree whose branch diverges from main but carries no unique content — the state a rebasing land leaves behind, where the remedy is reset and `land` is both wrong and potentially destructive. Always creates a backup branch first (`--no-backup` to opt out): safety is the default, danger is the flag, and a branch ref costs 41 bytes. Deliberately NOT `--hard|--soft` — git's reset modes describe what happens to the index and working tree, but here the working tree is clean by definition and the only axis is whether an escape hatch is kept. Chosen as its own verb rather than `worktree reconcile --reset` because E-1882's classifier bails on any non-endless-managed file (169 differ in the motivating case), so shipping it as a reconcile flag would attach the fix to a command whose spec refuses to run it. Blocked by E-1940: the content-based risk predicate is the guard that makes reset refuse when the branch holds genuine work.

title.current: Convert UTC timestamps to local time on display across the CLI
title.proposed: Convert UTC timestamps to local time on display

description.current: Endless writes every timestamp as UTC (`datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime(...)`, ~20 call sites) and never converts on display — no `astimezone`, `localtime` or `fromtimestamp` anywhere in src/endless. Every date the CLI shows is therefore UTC rendered as if local: verified, E-1978's stored created_at is 2026-08-15T09:43:08 while the wall clock read 05:43 EDT, and `task show` printed '9:43 am'. This is not merely a footgun when correlating endless output with `git reflog` (which prints local) — it is wrong on its own terms for every user outside UTC, on every task, session, note and decision displayed, and it silently makes effects look like they precede causes. Fix at the display boundary, not in storage: keep storing UTC, convert to the operator's zone when formatting, and decide whether to print the zone abbreviation so values are self-describing. The stored format carries no offset, so parsing must assume UTC explicitly rather than rely on naive-datetime defaults.

title.current: Add an out-of-band feedback channel the agent cannot see
title.proposed: Add an out-of-band feedback channel the agent cannot see

description.current: ED-1555 fixes the label MECHANISM as in-band $TOKEN "quoted span" typed into a prompt. In-band is exactly what makes feedback unusable in practice: anything in the conversation is visible by construction, so the agent comments on the critique — which is the behaviour the critique is usually about. A `!` shell call does not help (tested: the agent still replies), and a skill cannot help either, since 'run this and say nothing' is a guideline and this project's thesis is that guidelines lose to gates. The only structurally silent channel is out-of-band: `endless feedback` run in a sibling terminal pane, which Claude never sees. Needs the CLI (free-form critique, optional span reference, silent on success, LOUD on any rejection), and a slash-command front door for users who will not use a terminal, accepting that it comments. Evidence in --analysis.

title.current: Diagnose a stale sandbox DB instead of leaking a raw SQL error
title.proposed: Diagnose a stale sandbox DB instead of a raw SQL error

The message should name the DB file, say how far behind it is, and name the fix (--db main, or re-provision). Relates to E-1964, which relocates sandboxes and will not by itself make a stale one legible.

title.current: Use /proc instead of lsof for the live-process probe where available
title.proposed: Use /proc instead of lsof for the live-process probe

description.current: monitor.hasLiveProcessInDir — the "is a process standing in this worktree" half of monitor.WorktreeInUse (E-1947) — shells to `lsof -t -a -d cwd +D <dir>`. lsof is absent on minimal Linux images (Alpine, slim Debian), where the probe errors, WorktreeInUse fails closed, and `worktree drop` refuses on every worktree without --force while the reaper skips every candidate. Unreachable on macOS (lsof ships at /usr/sbin/lsof), but Linux is now real: the first beta user can run Endless there. Fix is capability detection, not OS dispatch — if /proc exists, readlink /proc/<pid>/cwd and prefix-match; otherwise lsof as today. No external binary on Linux, and faster than lsof, whose +D walks the whole worktree tree.

The list must be extensible from config, since one user's container directory is another's layout. Soft-deleting projects is NOT in scope here — that is E-2010.

title.current: Store project paths home-relative so ad-hoc SQL over the ledger stays readable
title.proposed: Store project paths home-relative

description.current: Implements ED-1562 as amended. E-2002 made both halves normalize identically; this re-points the canonical form from absolute to home-relative (tilde prefix), keeping absolute only for paths outside $HOME. The point is legibility of 'endless sql' output, which is a supported surface. The trap to design around: today one function returns the canonical form AND that value is passed to os.Stat, filepath.Join and git. A tilde string is not a filesystem path in Go or Python, so the single accessor must split in two — a STORED form (home-relative, used for writes and comparisons) and a RESOLVED form (absolute, used for anything touching disk) — with names that make the difference obvious at the call site. Comparisons happen in stored form; symlinks are still resolved before relativizing. A change file rewrites existing rows, as E-2002's did. $HOME being unset or wrong must fail loudly, never silently yield a bad path.

title.current: Fix just land's landing-record failure when the branch renames a Python symbol
title.proposed: Fix land's record failure on a Python symbol rename

description.current: `endless worktree land` runs from the main checkout's editable install and ff-merges main underneath its own live process, so modules imported AFTER the merge come from the new source while ones already in sys.modules stay at the old one. A branch that renames a Python symbol therefore breaks a post-merge lazy import: E-2011 renamed endless.project_path.normalize to resolved, main advanced, and recording the landing died on `cannot import name 'resolved' from 'endless.project_path'` — leaving no task_landings row and the branch tip unmerged. Re-running lands cleanly because a fresh process loads the new source throughout, so this is a half-completed land and a confusing error, not corruption. self_dev-only (a downstream land does not replace endless's own code), but every self_dev land of a Python rename is exposed.

title.current: Enforce the documented status lifecycle on task update
title.proposed: Enforce the documented status lifecycle on task update

description.current: Nothing enforces the documented status lifecycle. `task update --status` accepts any status from any status, from any actor, regardless of whether a session ever claimed the task. The lifecycle is byte-synced across three docs by a test while nothing checks the lifecycle itself. Natural home is E-1891's status registry.

description.current: Implements ED-1565. description.current: Implements ED-1567 and ED-1570. Stop monitor.DB() applying schema on connect; compare the DB's goose version against the binary's and require exact agreement. (3) db.py's _incomplete_schema_hint points at a change file -- deferred to E-2158, which deletes its subject.

title.current: Decide the non-self_dev upgrade policy and the schema compatibility range
title.proposed: Decide the upgrade policy and schema compatibility range

description.current: ED-1567 settled that ordinary connects verify and refuse, confirmed for self_dev. Two questions remain and they are entangled. (1) A normal user has one installed binary, so the two-binary problem does not arise; on a mismatch after upgrading endless, does that binary refuse (uniform behavior, one tested path, an extra step after every upgrade) or auto-upgrade forward (no interruption, but preserves the 'any binary may migrate whatever DB it opens' property this decision exists to remove)? (2) ED-1568 made expand-contract a rule, and it only pays off if the connect check admits a compatibility RANGE rather than an exact match -- goose gives a linear version, so two schema-compatible binaries compare unequal and refuse anyway. Binaries need to declare the range they support. How harsh the refusal must be depends on how often a mismatch can happen at all, which is what the range determines.

title.current: Restart background agents and jobs onto the new binary after a schema upgrade
title.proposed: Restart agents and jobs onto the new binary after upgrade

description.current: ED-1570 halts a binary whose schema version is behind the database. After an upgrade migrates the ledger, every long-running process still holding the old binary image — background agents, the jobs runner — halts on its next connect and dies mid-flight, which can take down tens of live sessions at once. Halting is correct and must not be relaxed, so the fix is on the other side: detect processes running a superseded binary and restart them onto the new one as part of the upgrade, rather than letting them discover the mismatch one by one. E-1704 is the surface that decides which binary a process should be running; it moves that choice into the binary itself via self-re-exec, governed by E-1972's verified-compatible policy.

title.current: Inject who-to-message context at the moment an action affects a live session's work
title.proposed: Inject who-to-message context on actions affecting sessions

description.current: A session cannot act on information it never considers. Today the who-to-talk-to data is available on request, which requires knowing the command exists AND thinking to run it at the right moment; the second half is where it fails. A standing roster in additionalContext is the wrong fix -- it bloats context and earns notice-blindness, and one session can spawn ten tasks. Inject instead at the moment an action is recognized as affecting another live session's work, carrying the reply affordance inline rather than a list of who exists. Transport-agnostic: this decides WHEN a session is told whom to reach, while E-1936 decides the transport it reaches them with.

title.current: Refuse to run a worktree binary against a main DB whose schema it cannot read

title.current: Stop losing why a decision stopped governing: require a reason, stop clearing reasons on reversal
title.proposed: Stop losing why a decision stopped governing

description.current: E-1920 shipped `decision supersede` with no way to say WHY a decision stopped governing, on the reasoning that the successor is the reason. That fails whenever the cause is a fact about the world rather than about the successor: ED-1067 was superseded by ED-1570 because both of ED-1067's consumers died, which ED-1570 does not say. Make --reason required, matching obsolete and reject. Separately, reversals destroy data on the common path: `unreject` clears rejection_reason (E-1864) and `reinstate` clears obsolete_reason (E-1920, copied from it), silently and unrecoverably. Both justifications were about RENDERING, so the fix is to keep the value and gate the display on status, not to add a --force. Third, supersede does not notice an existing `reverses` or `modifies` link between the pair, so ED-1067 now renders two links to ED-1570 that read as independent facts.

title.current: Add a ledger write-lease so land's rebase-to-fast-forward window cannot be raced by emitters
title.proposed: Add a ledger write-lease around land's fast-forward window

description.current: just land can fail all 8 retries because every ledger append amends main's tip SHA, invalidating the just-computed fast-forward; with several live sessions emitting, land may never converge. Add an automatic short-lived write-lease: land acquires it before its rebase/fast-forward window, every emitter checks it and briefly waits (bounded) instead of failing, land releases it on exit, and the lease self-expires so a crashed land cannot wedge writers. Chosen over a manual freeze switch in config, which a human must remember to set and unset while every other session fails mysteriously in between; the lease has no ceremony and behaves the same for any busy multi-session project.

title.current: Commit each lesson at write time so recording one never requires a land

description.current: E-2051 moved lesson appends to the main checkout, so writing a lesson no longer dirties a worktree. Retires E-2051's AUTO_COMMIT_GLOBS entry and its Go mirror, since nothing is left for land to sweep.

title.current: Reject a parent cycle on task update, not only on task move
title.proposed: Reject a parent cycle on task update, not only on task move

description.current: `endless task update --parent` can create a parent cycle; `endless task move` cannot. The two verbs write `tasks.parent_id` through different events: `move` emits `task.moved`, whose executor walks the ancestor chain and refuses a circular reference, while `update` emits `task.fields_updated`, whose executor carries `parent_id` in its allowedFields map and writes it with no such walk. Reproduced 2026-08-25 — setting E-799 parent to E-1935 while E-1935 parent was still E-799 produced 799 -> 1935 -> 799, and every recursive CTE over the task tree walks that forever. Lift the ancestor walk out of execTaskMoved into a shared validator and call it from both executors, exactly as ValidateMaybeParentless is already shared between them. The guard belongs in Go, where the write happens.

title.current: Announce a truncated list instead of cutting it off silently
title.proposed: Announce a truncated list instead of cutting it off silently

description.current: A list that gets cut off says nothing about it. `endless sql` and the listing verbs return every matching row with no cap, so a consumer that cannot predict the result size bounds it downstream with `head` — and `head` is silent, which makes a truncated result indistinguishable from a complete one. That silence turned two searches in one session into false "no existing task" conclusions: E-1935 fell off a `head -30` and E-1535 off a `head -24`, both ordered by id ASC so the newest and most relevant rows were exactly the ones dropped. Endless already has the right idiom — the session-status view never hides silently, printing "… N hidden (--show-hidden)". Give the listing surfaces a default cap that announces itself the same way, so the cap lives in the tool and describes itself instead of living in a pipe that cannot. Which commands need it is for the implementor to determine and confirm with the user.

title.current: Make the worktree-removal prohibition categorical in the handoff templates
title.proposed: Make the worktree-removal prohibition categorical

description.current: Every spawned session's handoff says "Don't run 'endless worktree land'/'drop' without asking." That form makes the session evaluate a precondition — have I been asked? — and that evaluation is where it fails: on 2026-08-25 two sessions destroyed worktrees within ten minutes, neither overriding the rule, both concluding the precondition was met by conversational text that did not meet it. One caused real damage. Split the two verbs: keep ask-first for land, which is the normal end of a task, and make removal categorical with no precondition to mis-evaluate. Six handoff templates carry the line, and the rule must name the outcome (drop, reap, git worktree remove) rather than one command, since a drop-only prohibition is satisfiable by another route.

title.current: Move per-task verify scripts out of tests/ so they cannot be swept up as a suite
title.proposed: Move per-task verify scripts out of tests/

description.current: Per-task verify scripts live in tests/tasks/*.sh, which makes them look like a test suite. They are not one: each drives real binaries (hook, endless-go, git, tmux) and several are not isolated from the live environment. Running e-1202-verify writes a session row into the MAIN database bound to the caller's actual tmux pane, after which two sessions claim one pane and every companion-resolving command, esu included, refuses to pick between them. The rule is that a session runs its OWN task's script and no other; the layout works against it, because any glob over tests/ sweeps them in. Move them somewhere that does not read as a suite, and make the mistake structurally hard rather than merely forbidden.

title.current: Project verbs.jsonl shadows the built-in defaults instead of layering over them
title.proposed: Project verbs.jsonl shadows the built-in defaults

description.current: matchers._resolved_verbs() returns the FIRST source that exists — project, else machine, else DEFAULT_VERBS — rather than merging them. title.current: Canonicalize the verify runner's temp HOME so suites stop failing on a symlinked macOS temp root
title.proposed: Canonicalize the verify runner's temp HOME

description.current: Repointed: the test is not where this belongs. E-2023's runner hands every suite a temp HOME from os.MkdirTemp, and on macOS the OS temp root sits beneath a symlinked prefix (var -> private/var) — so every suite runs under a HOME reached through a symlink, which a real home directory almost never is. title.current: Surface worktree drift continuously instead of relying on someone remembering to sweep
title.proposed: Surface worktree drift continuously

description.current: `endless worktree sync` reports and closes worktree drift, but only when a person runs it. title.current: Explore what an Endless session is without Claude and without tmux
title.proposed: Explore an Endless session without Claude or tmux

description.current: Endless assumes Claude and tmux so foundationally that the agent-less path is barely designed: claim --unattended claims a task and leaves sessions.task_id unset, so the work has no session record and no route back. If a session record is the spine, then what is absent in that case is an AGENT, not a session — which argues the flag should be --no-agent and should still mint a session, and raises the question of what a non-Claude session row holds and how it starts and ends. Map what breaks without tmux (goto, resume, monitor, status line) and without Claude (transcripts, hooks, handoff, spawn) before changing anything. Expect a follow-up research task. The --unattended rename rides along rather than landing first, since renaming a flag before deciding whether the concept survives is churn.

title.current: Run database backups on a schedule with tiered retention, not only before migrations
title.proposed: Run database backups on a schedule with tiered retention

description.current: Backups only run before a schema migration: _backup_db has exactly one caller, and the Go path fires only from the pre-apply step during land and from an explicit endless db backup. So the newest backup can be weeks old — it was nine days stale when it was needed. The docstring's 'if last backup is > 60 seconds old' reads like a frequency but is only a throttle on a rare event. Register a backup job in the internal/jobs registry the way triagejob and minimizerjob do, so session monitor fires it on a schedule, and replace the keep-last-60-by-count rotation with tiered retention: hourly for 24 hours, then daily for 30 days, then weekly for a year.

title.current: Report what git actually said when worktree land's rebase fails

description.current: `worktree land` treats any non-zero exit from `git rebase` as a content conflict, so a rebase that stopped for another reason reports 'rebase conflict' with 'Conflicting files: (none reported)' and recovery candidates for a cause it never established. description.current: 'endless task show <id> --json' returns "analysis": null for a field holding 6503 characters, because the display flags that gate the human renderer also gate the JSON payload. E-1601 specified that deliberately; this task revisits it for the machine format only. A consumer that does not pass a display flag reads a populated task as empty, and 'null' means both 'empty' and 'withheld' — indistinguishable for description, which has no _chars companion. Fix: --json returns full bodies by default, and a new --brief[=N] opts into a light payload by truncating to 256 chars with an ellipsis rather than omitting, so a populated field is always a string and null means only 'empty'. Folded in while task show is open: children render before the long text fields rather than last, and a 'Children: 5 tasks (3 todo, 2 bugfix)' line appears whenever children exist, with children_count and children_by_type in the machine formats.

title.current: Share one per-repo patch-id index across worktrees instead of recomputing base patch-ids per probe
title.proposed: Share one per-repo patch-id index across worktrees

description.current: The exact unlanded probe's cost is dominated by computing patch-ids for every commit the base gained since a worktree's fork, and every worktree recomputes them against substantially the same base history — measured 584ms for e-1077 against 135 worktrees that share one main. Build the index once per repo under <git-common-dir>/info/endless, appended incrementally as the base grows, so each worktree pays only for its own handful of commits: O(base commits + sum of branch commits) instead of O(worktrees x base commits). range-diff's similarity pairing, which is what catches a conflict-resolved landing, would run as a second stage over only the unmatched residue. Deferred from E-2111 deliberately: with the verdict computed by a background job and a settled verdict surviving base movement, every miss is off the critical path and cold-miss storms are small. Measure first; build only if misses actually hurt. Invalidation rides the same base-tip watermark E-2111 introduces.

title.current: Compute the exact unlanded verdict in one background job and read it from a content-addressed cache
title.proposed: Compute the exact unlanded verdict in one background job

description.current: This task conforms to decision ED-1589. The exact 'does this branch hold work the base lacks?' probe (git range-diff, measured 584ms per worktree) is recomputed by every consumer on every tick: the reaper on five hook branches including PreToolUse and PostToolUse, and every session monitor pane re-probing every rendered row every two seconds. Move it behind one background job that writes a content-addressed cache under the git common dir, and make the display path read-only with a fourth marker state for 'not yet determined'. Delete the five hook-path reaper calls; the reaper keeps its existing trigger, the post-land sweep worktree land already runs, and gains an exact condition 4 that reads the cache. Restores agreement between the reaper, the diamond marker and 'task unsettled' about what landed, which the E-2087 hotfix broke on purpose, and closes the reclamation leak it accepted.

title.current: Rebase idle worktree branches onto the base branch on a cadence to stop drift accumulating
title.proposed: Rebase idle worktree branches onto the base on a cadence

description.current: E-1881's counterpart and the other half of keeping worktrees in sync: E-1881 moves endless-managed metadata commits UP to main, which is what lets a worktree settle and become reclaimable; this is the DOWN direction, rebasing each idle worktree branch onto the base so the merge base moves forward. That collapses the range the exact unlanded probe pays for — its cost is proportional to how far the base drifted since the fork, not to what the branch holds — and makes a later land a fast-forward. Blocked by E-1881 rather than merely related: without it the branch still holds metadata commits main changed independently, so a rebase hits exactly the conflicts E-1882 exists to resolve by hand. Hard constraint: idle worktrees only, via the WorktreeInUse predicate the reaper shares with the other destructive path (E-1947).

title.current: Propagate an interrupted git child through DefaultBranch so a Ctrl-C does not record ERR-0011
title.proposed: Propagate an interrupted git child through DefaultBranch

description.current: DefaultBranch collapses every git error into ErrDefaultBranchUnresolved, so a git child interrupted during default-branch resolution records ERR-0011 — the misclassification E-2113 removed for ERR-0010, surviving under a different error code. defaultBranchCache then memoizes that failure, so one Ctrl-C poisons every later probe in the process rather than costing one tick. E-2113's guards on the two default-branch fault recorders are correct but unreachable until the resolver stops swallowing the interrupt.

title.current: Render a task's decision relations in task show
title.proposed: Render a task's decision relations in task show

description.current: endless task show renders task-to-task relations only. A decision linked to a task — documents, implemented_by, relates_to — is visible from decision show but invisible from the task, so a session reading its own task cannot see which decisions bind it. ED-1589 links to E-2128 as implemented_by and does not appear anywhere in 'task show E-2128'. This is why tasks acquired the prose habit of opening with 'Implements ED-NNNN': the banner was carrying information the view refused to render. That convention is now banned, which makes this gap load-bearing rather than cosmetic. Render decision links in the same relations block as task links, distinguished by the ED- prefix they already carry. Check task show --all-fields and the JSON output for the same omission.

title.current: Require an explicit DB context everywhere, and make every read state the one it used
title.proposed: Require an explicit DB context and state it on every read

description.current: A command's DB context can be GUESSED and the answer never says which one it used. Both halves are one omission: monitor.guardWorktreeDBContext already refuses to open the DB inside a self-dev worktree with no explicit context, and already names the remedy, but dbContextExplicit() is 'dbContextDir != "" || dbPathOverride != ""' and main.go calls SelfDetectWorktreeSandbox() for every subcommand, so CWD satisfies a gate whose own comment says only a flag counts. Fix both: require dbContextFromFlag (already tracked, never consulted) so only a per-invocation flag authorises opening the DB, and make every read state the database and project it answered from.

title.current: Install Endless's Claude Code hooks in the project, not on the user machine
title.proposed: Install Endless's Claude Code hooks per project

description.current: Endless installs its hooks machine-wide in the user's Claude Code settings, so every session in every directory invokes endless-go on every hooked event — including projects that will never use Endless. That forces a runtime bypass to exist and stay correct, when an unregistered hook simply cannot fire. Move installation to the project's own .claude/settings.json via 'project init', with a committed project-relative loader script so the file carries no machine-specific path, and migrate off the user-level entries so tracked projects do not double-fire.

title.current: Decide how to make folding a finding cheaper than filing it as a second task
title.proposed: Decide how to make folding a finding cheaper than filing it

description.current: ED-1550 wants a finding folded into an existing task rather than filed as a new one, but the tooling inverts the incentive: filing is one command, folding afterwards is four plus a content merge, and the same-session root-cause hint fires only AFTER the task already exists. Live case: a session filed two tasks for one cause, wrote the shared cause into the second task's own analysis, read the hint, answered it in prose, and filed anyway. Brainstorm which intervention actually binds an agent — gate the second 'task add' in a session and demand a disposition, add a one-command fold that merges and closes, reword the hint so its test cannot be escaped by disputing the word 'symptom' — and what each costs.

title.current: Emit agent-facing output as TOON: add the emitter and settle the shape rules
title.proposed: Emit agent-facing output as TOON

description.current: E-1504 sweeps 31 commands to offer an agent-facing text view; this settles what that view IS, and lands first so those renderings are written once rather than twice. Deliver a TOON emitter for the Python CLI plus the shape rules it applies: which commands are list-shaped (arrays of uniform objects, where TOON declares fields once and emits a row per record — the whole reason to adopt it) versus detail-shaped (one object of long prose fields, where the saving is small), how prose and empty fields render, a key vocabulary shared across commands, no truncation, and glyph-encoded signals promoted to explicit fields. Only the stable Python implementation is needed: Go's JSON is internal plumbing consumed by Python, not read by an agent, so TOON's in-development Go implementation blocks nothing. title.current: Write task doc mirrors to main, then consolidate them under .endless/tasks/e-nnnn/
title.proposed: Write task doc mirrors to main, then consolidate them

description.current: Endless writes a task's content twice: the ledger entry, enforced to land on main only, and a human-readable mirror under .endless/plans|analyses|outcomes|decisions, which goes to the task BRANCH and waits for a land. Measured over 133 worktrees: 123 of the 139 genuinely-unlanded commits are doc-mirror commits, and 44 of 56 unlanded worktrees are unlanded only because of them. Phase A writes the mirror to main at write time, stops materializing mirrors into worktrees, and drains the 123 commits off branches — which makes E-1881's step 1 unnecessary rather than automated. Phase B, absorbed from E-2138, then consolidates the files into .endless/tasks/e-nnnn/<type>.md, the directory that already holds each task's verify.sh, replacing a directory allowlist that has already gone stale once with a single glob. The order is not optional: git's directory-rename detection places a branch's new file inside another task's directory, so the drain must precede the rename.

title.current: Define obsolete as what the word means, not as it never needed doing

description.current: Endless glosses the obsolete status as 'Made irrelevant by other changes -- it never needed doing', and every transition into it carries the label 'retires -- it never needed doing' in the Go transition table. title.current: Handle StopFailure: a turn that dies on an API error must leave the session honest
title.proposed: Handle Claude Code's StopFailure hook event

description.current: End-of-turn handling is attached to ONE event when Claude Code has TWO. Everything Endless does when a turn ends hangs off the Stop case — ParseTranscript then IdleSession — but Claude Code fires StopFailure INSTEAD OF Stop when a turn dies on an API error (rate_limit, overloaded, max_output_tokens, server_error and others). So a failed turn takes none of that handling with it: the transcript is unparsed and the session never leaves 'working'. Nothing else moves it — SessionEnd fires on session termination, TouchSession never clobbers a live state, and liveness sees a pane that is still there. The board then asserts work is in flight on a dead turn, and auto-spawn's cap throttles against sessions that are gone. Install the event AND handle it: installing alone leaves the session 'working' with a freshly refreshed last_activity, which is worse. Idle the session, parse the transcript, and record the error type as a fault. No new session state.

title.current: Decide how Endless detects and handles code running from a stale binary

title.current: Refuse user-only commands and status transitions when an agent is the actor
title.proposed: Refuse user-only commands when an agent is the actor

description.current: Endless treats some acts as the user's — worktree drop, event rebuild-db --confirm, db restore, project unregister --purge, and the setup commands that write shell rc files and global Claude settings — but enforces that only by convention and message wording. Agent detection already exists (agent_env.present / agentenv.Present, keyed on the Claude Code environment), so those commands refuse an agent outright: the refusal says to run it from a terminal outside the session, and is REPORT-class per E-2159. User-owned status transitions are NOT refused outright, because the user routinely asks an agent to record a decision and write the outcome prose; instead an agent taking a user edge must carry a non-empty --outcome in the same event, so a bare status flip nobody decided is refused. task approve and decision accept/reject have no outcome to carry and so stay user-only until E-2047 gives them a reason.

title.proposed: Let session resume re-enter a crash-restored tmux window

description.current: After a tmux crash, tmux-resurrect restores windows, panes, layouts and cwds but NOT the `@endless_*` window options — verified against a real save file, which contains zero `@endless` strings. title.current: Add a top-level touch command that puts a task in the session's scope
title.proposed: Add a top-level touch command for session scope

description.current: There is no way to add a task to session_tasks — to make it appear in session status — without editing the task itself. The workaround in use is to change a field that does not need changing, most often phase, purely for the touch side effect: 'I set to now but only because updating a task is how I add a task to session status.' That writes a real field change into the ledger to buy a display effect, so the task's recorded phase stops meaning what it says, and a later reader cannot tell a deliberate re-prioritization from a side-channel. It also fires a change notice to every other session holding the task. A verb whose whole job is scope entry removes the incentive: touch a task, it joins session_tasks with the revisited relation, nothing about the task changes. Top-level rather than under session or task: many subcommands are slated to move to top level, so placing it under a parent now only schedules a rename.

title.current: Name a spawned session after its task
title.proposed: Name a spawned session after its task

description.current: endless task spawn never passes claude --name, so a spawned session falls back to Claude Code's default: the worktree basename plus a two-character disambiguator, e.g. e-1983-f2. Default spawn_plan's name parameter to e-{item_id} and it becomes e-1983. The whole path already exists and is used by the explicit --name flag; only the default is missing. Matters because ListAgents and SendMessage address sessions by name, which is the transport E-1995 depends on, so the name is an address rather than a label. E-2102 already settled the same question for tmux window names.

title.current: Stop just install re-pinning a worktree's Claude hooks when its branch predates the fix
title.proposed: Stop just install re-pinning worktree Claude hooks

description.current: A worktree-scoped `just install` calls go-work-init, build, dev-sandbox-init and claude-settings-init with a bare `just`, which resolves the WORKTREE's justfile — so running it in any of the ~99 branches cut before E-2166 landed re-pins that worktree's hooks at its own bin/endless-go. Resolve the machine-level CONFIG recipes from main's justfile as post-worktree-create.sh already does, leaving `build` on the branch because a worktree exists to build candidate code. Then delete the one-time claude-settings-sweep recipe E-2166 added, once `endless worktree sync --apply` has delivered the fixed recipe to live branches. Self_dev only (ED-1571).
